6.1. Add 250μL of solution C2 to the supernatant. Vortex for 5 seconds.

7. Centrifugation and Further Processing.
7.1. Centrifuge at 10,000g for 1 minute at room temperature.

9.2. Transfer 750μL of supernatant to a clean 2mL collection tube.
10. Solution C4 Addition and Mixing.
10.1. Add 1200μL of solution C4 (shake to mix before use). Vortex for 5 seconds.
11. Spin Filter Processing.
11.1. Load 675μL of the mixture into a spin filter. Centrifuge at 10,000g for 1 minute at room temperature. Discard the flow through.
11.2. Add another 675μL to the spin filter. Centrifuge at 10,000g for 1 minute at room temperature. Discard the flow through.
11.3. Load the remaining supernatant into the spin filter. Centrifuge at 10,000g for 1 minute at room temperature. Discard the flow through.
12. Final Wash and Elution.
12.1. Add 500μL of solution C5 to the spin filter. Centrifuge at 10,000g for 30 seconds at room temperature.
12.2. Discard the flow through.
12.3. Centrifuge again at 10,000g for 1 minute at room temperature.
13. DNA Recovery and Storage.
13.1. Place the spin filter in a clean 2mL collection tube.
13.2. Add 60μL of nuclease-free water to the center of the white filter membrane. Adjust the volume based on expected yield and desired DNA concentration. Let sit for 5 minutes.
13.3. Centrifuge at 10,000g for 30 seconds at room temperature.
13.4. Discard the spin filter. Aliquot the DNA for Qubit and PCR analysis.
13.5. Store the remaining DNA sample at -20°C for short-term storage or -80°C for long-term storage.

instruction: Please describe the protocol in a two-level list format (using 1., 2., 3. numbers, with one-level sub-steps). Include only the steps, not a rationale or materials list. Use concise language and maintain a chronological order.
input: The objective is to determine chlorophyll concentration using CuSO4 magnesium-copper exchange titration. Have prepared sample plant matter, crystals, and necessary solutions. Now, how to perform the extraction and titration process?
output: 1. Prepare the sample and extraction.
1.1. Add 2g of sample plant matter or other test article to a mortar.
1.2. Add 1g of crystals to the mortar.
1.3. Grind the sample item and together until the leaves are ground up, the magnesium sulfate is completely dissolved into the plant liquid, and a liquid starts to form.
1.4. Transfer as much of the solid and liquid slurry to a 20ml test tube.
1.5. Add 8mL to the 20ml test tube. This is the raw mix.
1.6. Add 1mL of to the mortar to wash up and collect as much of the sample as possible into the 20ml test tube.

1.7. Use a glass stirrer to stir the raw mix. Take care to press the plant slurry down to the base of the test tube, then agitate the slurry again to mix. Repeat this many times for 120s minutes. Ensure that the acetone is fully incorporated into the slurry.
1.8. Let the raw mix stand for 300s minutes.
1.9. Use a glass stirrer to stir the raw mix again for 60s minute.
1.10. Use a 20 micron retention filtration paper to filter the raw mix into another test tube. Ensure to use a new filter paper for each separate sample. This is the refined mix.
2. Dilution phase.

2.1. Determine the resolution needed for the concentration. The resolution is the interval of dilution. For example, a 10% resolution will result in a dilution interval of 100%, 90%, 80%, etc. The smaller the resolution the narrower the margin of error is. For this protocol, the resolution used will be 10%.
2.2. Label ten 5ml vials in descending order from 100% to 10%.

2.3. Add Acid Activated mix to each 5ml vial at volume based on the formula Vol = 1000ul * Per with Per representing the percentage written on each vial. Use the percentage or decimal, not whole number. Ex. 10% = .10
3. Copper transfer phase.
3.1. Prepare a 60mgCuSO4/mlH2O concentration solution to be referred to as the copper (II) sulfate Solution.
4. Acid activation.
4.1. Add 1mL to the refined mix and mix with clean glass stirrer for 60s minute to create the Acid Activated Mix.
4.2. Let the Acid Activated Mix stand for 120s minutes.
5. Titration phase.
5.1. Add 100 µL copper (II) sulfate Solution to each PCR tube.

Prepare calibration standards solutions for HPLC by diluting 200ul of the calibration stock solutions in sequence with 200ul of methanol and 1.0ml of water.   1.3. Sample Storage.     1.3.1. Seal all samples and calibration standards in an HPLC vial and store them in a refrigerator between 3 and 8°C until analysis. 2. Measurement.   2.1. HPLC-UV System Conditioning.     2.1.1. Dissolve the dried plant extracts (2.5mg) in 1ml of aqueous acetone (50%) and sonicate (35kHz, 250W) at room temperature for 30 minutes.     3.1.2. Prepare a matrix solution by dissolving 10mg of 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid in 1ml of pure acetone.     3.1.3. Mix 10ul of the extract solution with 10ul of matrix solution and spike it with 1ul of KCl (10mM in water).     3.1.4. Deposit 5ul of the mixture on the MALDI-TOF stainless steel plate and allow it to dry at room temperature for about 1 hour.   3.2. Measurement.     3.2.1. input: To assess the biocompatibility of chemical reactions in biochemical applications by simulating cellular environments. Available materials: para-toluenesulfonanilide, diphenyliodonium chloride, potassium phosphate, copper(I) chloride, ddH2O, bio-additives (BSA, RNase A), Celite plugs, GC-FID, UHPLC-MS, SDS-PAGE, and RNA gels. output: 1. Reaction Setup.   1.1. Add 24.7 mg of para-toluenesulfonanilide, 38 mg of diphenyliodonium chloride, and 42.5 mg of potassium phosphate to a 4-mL reaction vessel with a 5-mm PTFE magnetic stir bar.   1.2. For each solid additive in Group I, weigh 1.0 equiv. and add to the reaction vessel.   1.3. Add 2.0 mg of copper(I) chloride to the reaction vessel. 2. Reaction Procedure for Group I Additives.   2.1. Add 1.5 mL of ddH2O using a 1-mL pipette to dissolve the reagents.   2.2. Add 1.0 equiv. of liquid bio-additive using a suitable pipette.   2.3. Seal the glass vessel and shake thoroughly.   2.4. Incubate by stirring (~1,000 r.p.m.) at RT for 15 h.   2.5. Transfer 150 µL of the reaction mixture to a 1.5-mL reaction vessel for biomolecule preservation analysis. 3. Reaction Procedure for Group II Additives.   3.1. Prepare a 100 µM stock solution of bio-additive (BSA and RNase A) and store on ice.   3.2. Repeat Steps 1-3 for all additives in Group II.   3.3. Add ddH2O to the glass vessel with reagents to reach a final volume of 1.5 mL.   3.4. Add appropriate volumes of additives to reach the final concentration.   3.5. Repeat the Group I procedure. 4. Analysis of Biomolecule Preservation.   4.1. Determination of Starting Material and Reaction Yield by GC-FID.     4.1.1. Prepare Celite plugs for filtration.     4.1.2. Add 12.6 µL of mesitylene and 2 mL of acetone to each reaction vessel, seal, and shake thoroughly.     4.1.3. Transfer 200 µL of each reaction to the respective Celite plug and allow adsorption.     4.1.4. Analyze each sample using GC.     4.1.5. Determine peak areas for product, starting material, and internal standard.   4.2. Qualitative Analysis of Biomolecule Preservation using UHPLC-MS.     4.2.1. Centrifuge the aliquot for 10-15 min at 4 °C at 21,000g.     4.2.2. Prepare a glass vial with a micro insert.     4.2.3. Pipette 35 µL of the supernatant into the insert for a 30 µL injection.     4.2.4. Prepare untreated bio-additive controls dissolved in ddH2O.     4.2.5. Set up the UHPLC-MS system for sample characterization.   4.3. Gel Electrophoretic Analysis of Protein Biomolecule Preservation in Group II Samples.     4.3.1. Prepare samples with 1 µg of protein and 3× loading buffer.     4.3.2. Heat samples at 95 °C for 5 min.     4.3.3. Prepare the gel electrophoresis apparatus with protein gel.     4.3.4. Load PageRuler prestained protein ladder and samples into the gel.     4.3.5. Run the gel at 100 V for 10-20 min, then at 120 V for 1-1.5 h.   4.4. Gel Electrophoretic Analysis of Group II Nucleic Acids.     4.4.1. Add ddH2O to 150 µL aliquots of nucleic acids to 400 µL final volume.     4.4.2. Add 40 µL of 3 M NaOAc, 1 µL of glycogen, and 1,320 µL of 100% EtOH.     4.4.3. Centrifuge for at least 1 h at 4 °C at 21,000g.     4.4.4. Prepare gels according to the manufacturer's instructions.     4.4.5. Load appropriate volumes of ladder and samples into the gel. 5. Preparation of Cell Lysate.   5.1. Culture cells in two 10-cm Petri dishes to 80% confluency.   5.2. Aspirate the medium and wash cells with 10 mL of 1× PBS.   5.3. Aspirate PBS and add 1.5 mL of CelLytic M reagent to each dish.   5.4. Incubate for 15 min at RT on a platform shaker.   5.5. Prepare six clean 1.5-mL reaction vessels and place them on ice. 6. Isolation of Total RNA.   6.1. Culture cells in 1 well of a 6-well plate to 80% confluency.   6.2. Prepare 4:1 and 2:1 phenol/chloroform mixtures immediately before isolation and cool to 4 °C.   6.3. Aspirate medium, add 1 mL of lysis buffer, pipette up and down five times, and incubate for 2 min at RT.   6.4. Pipette lysate up and down five times and add to the 4:1 phenol/chloroform mixture.   6.5. Centrifuge for 3 min at RT at 21,000g. 7. Gel Preparation for SDS-PAGE and PAA Electrophoresis.   7.1. Assemble gel-casting modules according to the manufacturer's instructions.   7.2. For separating gel, add 4 mL ddH2O, 3.4 mL Rotiphorese Gel 30, 2.5 mL separating buffer, and 10 µL TEMED, mix gently.   7.3. Add 100 µL 10% APS and mix gently.   7.4. Cast both gels up to 5.5 cm and add 100 µL of 2-propanol on top.   7.5. Wait 20-30 min until polymerization is complete.

Exclude theoretical explanations. Format steps as: [MainStep] [SubStep] [SubSubStep] with numeric identifiers.
input: To detect and quantify SARS-CoV-2 in wastewater using ultrafiltration, silica column-based purification, and droplet digital reverse transcription PCR (ddRT-PCR). Available materials include Bovine Coronavirus (BCoV) spike, silica columns, ddPCR reagents. How to prepare samples, concentrate virus, extract RNA, set up ddPCR reactions, and analyze data?
output: 1. Preparation.

1.1. Sample Description and Treatment: Use untreated influent from wastewater treatment plants, provided in 50ml conical tubes (~40ml per tube). Optimal samples are flow proportional, collected over 24 hours, and stored at ~4°C. Protocol also suits grab samples from sewers.

1.2. Work Area Set Up: Wipe Biosafety Cabinet with 70% ethanol. Thaw BCoV spike (14.5μl per sample) and store on ice. Perform Innovaprep Start Up Procedure, insert effluent tube into 10% bleach. Ensure Elution Fluid, Ultrafiltration Tips, etc., are available.

1.3. Bovine Coronavirus Spike-In: Reconstitute lyophilized BCoV (10 doses) in 5ml PBS with 0.01% Tween 20. Prepare working stock (1:500 dilution) in 500μl aliquots at -80°C, targeting ~3000 genome copies/μl.
2. Clarification and Concentration of Wastewater.
2.1. Sample Pre-Treatment: Add BCoV spike (~14.3μl) and Tween-20 (400μl) to each sample. Adjust volume to 40ml, mix well, and store on ice until Step 6.
3. Filtration.
3.1. Filter each sample through a 0.22μm PES filter (>8cm diameter) to remove particulates and prevent ultrafiltration clogging.

3.2. Innovaprep Ultrafiltration: Insert ultrafiltration tip, start run. If run stops prematurely, press Return and restart. Transfer eluate to 15ml conical tubes, store on ice. Transfer 140μl eluate to AVL buffer (560μl) for RNA extraction.
4. Spike Lysis.
4.1. Add 5μl Quick Extract DNA Solution to 10μl BCoV Spike. Heat at 65°C for 15min, then 98°C for 2min. Add 85μl H2O and store on ice for ddPCR.
5. Extraction of RNA.

5.1. QiaAMP Viral RNA Extraction: After 10min incubation, add 560μl ethanol. Apply 630μl to Epoch column, centrifuge at 6000xg. Repeat steps with AW1 and AW2 buffers. Elute with 60μl RNase-free water, spin, and store samples.
6. Preparation for ddPCR.
6.1. SARS-CoV-2 Positive Control: Prepare diluted control (5μl Quick Extract + 10μl heat-inactivated virus), heat at 65°C for 15min, 98°C for 2min, dilute, aliquot, and store at -80°C.
6.2. Primer/Probe Mixes: Prepare mixes with 100μM Forward Primer, 100μM Reverse Primer, 100μM Probe, and H2O. Aliquot and store at -20°C in dark.
7. One-Step Reverse Transcription Droplet Digital PCR.

7.1. Reaction Set Up: Thaw reagents on ice. Prepare mastermix with Reverse Transcriptase, DTT, Primer/Probe Mixes, and BioRad supermix. Add template RNA to wells, pipette 13μl mastermix. Include positive and negative controls.
7.2. Droplet Generation: Transfer 20μl reactions to DG8 cartridge. Add 70μl AutoDG oil. Seal, insert into droplet generator, press Start. Transfer droplets to 96-well plate and seal.
7.3. Thermocycling: 50°C for 1hr (reverse transcription), 95°C for 10min, followed by 44 cycles of 94°C for 30sec and 55°C for 1min, then 98°C for 10min. Cool to 4°C.
7.4. Droplet Reading: Use QX200 reader. Select ABS, Ch1 FAM (SARS-CoV-2), Ch2 HEX (BCoV), and 1-step RT-ddPCR kit. Click RUN for analysis.
8. Data Analysis.
8.1. Set Thresholds in Quantasoft: Ensure droplet count exceeds 10,000. Position thresholds between positive and negative droplets in 2D Amplitude view.
8.2. Export Data to Excel: Export values including Well, Sample, Target, Copies/20μl, Accepted Droplets, PoissonConfMax, PoissonConfMin.
8.3. Calculate Genome Copies/L: Use formula with volumes of sample (40ml), eluate (200-900μl), RNA extraction (140μl), and reaction (8.2μl).
8.4. Endogenous Controls: Adjust calculations for diluted RNA (x100).
8.5. BCoV Recovery: Determine added BCoV copies and calculate recovery percentage.
8.6. Quality Controls: Monitor inhibition effects on RT and PCR steps. Use controls for normalization and troubleshooting.

output: 1. Precleavage Sample Preparation.   1.1 Flow-Wash Peptide-Resin.     1.1.1 Flow-wash peptide-resin with DMF for 30 s.   1.2 Dnp Deprotection.     1.2.1 Add 15 ml Dnp deprotection solution, react for 30 min, stir occasionally.     1.2.2 Drain solution, flow-wash with DMF for 30 s.     1.2.3 Repeat with another 15 ml Dnp solution, react for 30 min, stir occasionally.     1.2.4 Drain solution, flow-wash with DMF for 30 s.   1.3 Removal of N-Terminal Boc Group.     1.3.1 Drain DMF, add 5 ml TFA, drain immediately.     1.3.2 Add 5 ml TFA, react for 1 min.     1.3.3 Drain TFA.     1.3.4 Add 5 ml TFA, react for 5 min.     1.3.5 Drain TFA, flow-wash with DMF for 1 min.   1.4 Removal of Formyl Group of Tryptophan.     1.4.1 Add 10 ml acid neutralization solution, react for 1 min.     1.4.2 Drain, add another 10 ml acid neutralization solution, react for 1 min.     1.4.3 Drain, add 10 ml deformylation solution, react for 30 min, stir occasionally.     1.4.4 Drain, flow-wash with DMF for 30 s.     1.4.5 Drain, add another 10 ml deformylation solution, react for 30 min, stir occasionally.     1.4.6 Drain, flow-wash with DMF for 30 s.   1.5 Preparation of Resin for HF Cleavage.     1.5.1 Flow-wash with 50% dichloromethane/MeOH for 1 min, drain.     1.5.2 Dry resin under vacuum and N2 flow for 15 min.     1.5.3 Weigh resin into reaction vessel, up to 2 g capacity. 2. Complete HF Cleavage Procedure.   2.1 Equipment Preparation.     2.1.1 Prepare all equipment for HF cleavage.     2.1.2 Check CaO trap capacity for planned HF amount.   2.2 HF Cleavage Apparatus Preparation.     2.2.1 Turn on vacuum pump, evacuate HF cleavage apparatus.     2.2.2 Prepare 500 ml dry-ice/solvent mixture, fill three dewars.     2.2.3 Cool CV1 with dry-ice/solvent dewar for at least 15 min.   2.3 Reaction Vessel Preparation.     2.3.1 Prepare 700 ml warm tap water (25–50 °C).     2.3.2 Add scavenger to peptide-resin in reaction vessels.     2.3.3 Freeze scavenger-peptide-resin mixture with dry-ice for at least 5 min.     2.3.4 Add magnetic stir bar, close reaction vessel, attach to HF cleavage apparatus.   2.4 HF Cleavage.     2.4.1 Evacuate reaction vessels by opening taps 3 and 4.     2.4.2 Cool reaction vessels with dry-ice/solvent dewar for at least 10 min.     2.4.3 Double-check vacuum, dry ice, water bath temperature, and tap orientation.     2.4.4 Collect HF by closing tap 2, opening HF cylinder slowly to distill into CV1.     2.4.5 Close HF cylinder, open taps 1 and 3-6.     2.4.6 Heat CV1 with warm tap water bath, stir, warm HF for max 12 min.     2.4.7 Transfer HF to reaction vessels by closing taps 3 and 4, closing tap 5, opening tap 2, opening taps 3 and 4 simultaneously.   2.5 Cleavage Reaction.     2.5.1 Prepare water-ice-salt mixtures, exchange with reaction vessel dewars.     2.5.2 Start timer once peptide-resin-scavenger mixture thaws and suspends in HF.     2.5.3 Ensure reaction temperature stays between -5 and 0 °C.   2.6 Post-Cleavage Procedure.     2.6.1 Gradually open taps 3 and 4 clockwise to evaporate HF into CaO trap.     2.6.2 Prepare filtration setup, take cold diethyl ether from freezer.     2.6.3 Place reaction vessels into 500-ml water-ice beaker on magnetic stir plate.     2.6.4 Remove caps from reaction vessels, place into water-ice beaker to dilute HF traces. 3. Reaction Workup.   3.1 Filtration.     3.1.1 Filter reaction vessel solution, wash with another reaction vessel volume of cold diethyl ether.     3.1.2 Note filters may clog; use positive N2 pressure or new filter syringe.   3.2 Disposal and Lyophilization.     3.2.1 Dispose diethyl ether into plastic waste bottle.     3.2.2 Add lyophilization solution to dissolve peptide residue.     3.2.3 Transfer solution to filter syringe to dissolve remaining peptide.     3.2.4 Freeze peptide solution, put on lyophilizer.   3.3 Purification and Storage.     3.3.1 Run analytical RP-HPLC and MS to determine purity and confirm peptide mass.     3.3.2 Purify via (semi-) preparative RP-HPLC.     3.3.3 Store peptides at -20 °C for long-term storage.

input: The objective is to perform CUT&RUN on adherent cells in a multi-well cell culture plate. Have seeded cells in a 24-well plate and reached 70-90% confluence. Now, how to perform CUT&RUN including optional fixation?
output: 1. Cell seeding.
1.1. Seed adherent cells in a standard 24-well cell culture plate.
1.2. Seed the cells at an appropriate density so that the cells are 70 to 90% confluent when performing CUT&RUN.
2. CUT&RUN.
2.1. Perform CUT&RUN.
2.2. (Optional) Cells can be fixed by one of the following:
2.2.1. Fix intact cells by adding 500 μl of 1.5% formaldehyde (diluted in PBS) to a well and incubating for 10 min.
2.2.2. Wash cells ×3 with PBS and proceed to permeabilization.
2.2.3. Fix extracted cells by adding 500 μl Perm buffer to a well and incubating for 5 min.
2.2.4. Wash cells ×2 with PBS, add 500 μl of 1.5% formaldehyde (diluted in PBS), incubate for 10 min, and wash ×3 with PBS.
2.3. Permeabilization.
2.3.1. Dispense 500 μl Perm buffer per well and incubate on the bench (i.e., at room temperature) for 15 min.
2.3.2. Remove the buffer and wash the cells once with Perm buffer.
2.4. Antibody incubation.
2.4.1. Prepare antibody dilution in Perm buffer (150 μl per well).
2.4.2. Dispense 150 μl of the diluted antibody to a well and incubate on the bench for an hour.
2.4.3. Remove the antibody solution from the well and wash the cells ×2 with Perm buffer.
2.5. pAG-MNase incubation.
2.5.1. Prepare pAG-MNase dilution (1:33 volume) in 150 μl Perm buffer per well.
2.5.2. Dispense 150 μl of the diluted pAG-MNase into a well and incubate on the bench for an hour.
2.5.3. Remove the pAG-MNase solution from the well and wash the cells ×2 with Perm buffer.
2.6. Chromatin digestion.
2.6.1. Prepare Perm buffer containing 5 mM CaCl2 (add 1/20 volume of 100 mM CaCl2 to Perm buffer) and chill it on ice.
2.6.2. Make sure that the cells are chilled on ice-cold water.
2.6.3. Dispense 150 μl cold Perm buffer containing 5 mM CaCl2 and incubate the plate on ice-cold water for 30 min.
2.7. Fragment release.
2.7.1. Add 50 μl 4× STOP solution to a well (50 μl per well).
2.7.2. Gently rock the plate to mix the solution.
2.7.3. Place the cell culture plate in an incubator at 37°C for 30 min.
2.7.4. Collect the supernatant (∼200 μl).
2.8. Fragment purification.
2.8.1. If the cells were not fixed, purify the DNA fragment using DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (Qiagen, 69504).
2.8.2. If fixed, add 10 μl of 20% SDS to the supernatant (1% in final concentration) and incubate overnight at 65°C.
2.8.3. Add Proteinase K and incubate at 56°C for an hour.
2.8.4. Purify the DNA with QIAquick PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen, 28104).

Surgical Exposure of the Intact Primary Vein.   1.1 Select an expanded leaf and place the apical part of the leaf on a block of 1% (w/v) agar.   1.2 Make an arc-like incision through the upper (adaxial) and lateral epidermis of the petiole, 4-8 mm from the center of the rosette.   1.3 Make a second similar incision up to 4 mm from the first incision in the direction of the leaf tip.   1.4 Make a third cut through the adaxial (upper) epidermis to join the first incisions, taking care not to damage the vasculature.   1.5 Using small forceps and a scalpel, gently remove extravascular tissues from the region of the incisions to expose the vein. 2. Isolation of Intact Primary Vein Segments.   2.1 Select an expanded leaf and cut off the leaf blade with scissors just above the petiole/blade junction.   2.2 Make gentle incisions through the upper (adaxial) and lateral epidermis near the base of the petiole.   2.3 Gently pull away the cut end near the petiole/lamina junction to expose the midvein.   2.4 Quickly excise the vein for immediate use or rapid freezing in liquid nitrogen. 3. Extraction of Living Primary Veins Attached to the Leaf Base.   3.1 Make a ring-like incision through the upper (adaxial) and lateral epidermis of the petiole, 4-8 mm from the center of the rosette.   3.2 Gently pull away the leaf from the center of the plant to expose the attached midvein.   3.3 Place a block of 1% (w/v) agar in 0.5x Murashige Skoog (MS) medium (pH 5.7) on the soil below the exposed vein to prevent desiccation.   3.4 Optionally, place a strip of filter paper previously soaked in 0.5× MS medium on the agar block below the vein to enhance visibility.   3.5 Place the plants in the light in humidified Plexiglas boxes (30×20×20 cm) for 1 hour prior to experiments to allow recovery.

input: To extract high molecular weight (HMW) DNA from low amounts of fresh or herbarium lichen material. Available materials: MagMAX Microbiome Kit, Buffer 1, Buffer 2, Glucuronidase, Cellulase, Protoplast F, Lysozyme, Chitinase, Proteinase K, SPRIselect beads, PEG-NaCl-Buffer, 5 M NaCl, nuclease-free water. How to perform enzymatic digestion, size selection, and buffer preparation?
output: 1. ENZYMATIC DIGESTION - DAY 1.
1.1. Add 1 mL Buffer 1 to each sample.
1.1.1. Mix thoroughly by flipping the tube.
1.1.2. Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
1.1.3. Centrifuge at 3000 rpm for 2 minutes.
1.1.4. If necessary, repeat at a higher speed until a precipitate forms.
1.1.5. Discard supernatant.
1.2. Add 500 µL Buffer 2 to each sample.
1.2.1. Mix enzymes well before taking an aliquot.
1.2.2. Add 5 µL each of Glucuronidase, Cellulase, Protoplast F, and Lysozyme to each sample.
1.2.3. Add 90 µL Chitinase to each sample.
1.2.4. Place the tubes in a thermomixer overnight at 35 °C and rotate for 9 seconds every 5 minutes.
2. ENZYMATIC DIGESTION - DAY 2.
2.1. Set thermomixer to 56 °C.
2.1.1. Centrifuge samples with 3000 rpm for 2 minutes.
2.1.2. Discard supernatant while working under the fume hood.
2.1.3. Add 600 µL Buffer ATL and mix slowly and carefully.
2.1.4. Add 20 µL Proteinase K and mix slowly and carefully.
2.1.5. Incubate in a thermomixer at 56 °C with shaking for at least 1 hour.
2.1.6. Remove samples and set the thermomixer to 70 °C.
2.1.7. Briefly centrifuge tubes to remove drops from inside the lid.
2.1.8. Add 600 µL Buffer AL, close the lid, and mix gently using the lab rocker or by light shaking.
2.1.9. For low-input samples, dissolve 1 µg of carrier RNA in 1 µL of buffer ATL and add 1 µL of the dissolved carrier RNA to each sample.
2.1.10. Incubate tubes at 70 °C in a thermomixer with shaking at 600 rpm for 10 minutes.
2.1.11. Briefly centrifuge tubes to remove drops from inside the lid.
2.1.12. Add 300 µL ethanol (96-100%), close the lid, and mix by light shaking or on the lab rocker at 5 rpm for at least 10 seconds.
2.1.13. Mix samples and ethanol thoroughly to ensure efficient binding.
2.1.14. Briefly centrifuge tubes to remove drops from inside the lid.
2.1.15. Transfer 700 µL of the supernatant into a labelled 1.5 mL DNA LowBind tube.
2.1.16. Transfer the remaining ~800 µL into a second labelled tube, resulting in two storage vessels per sample.
3. EXTRACTION AND SIZE SELECTION.
3.1. Thoroughly shake the SPRIselect bottle to resuspend the SPRI beads.
3.1.1. Add *1.2 SPRIselect to the sample (sample volume [µL] * 1.2 = SPRIselect [µL]).
3.1.2. For long-read sequencing, add *0.65 of PEG-NaCl-Buffer (sample volume [µL] * 0.65 = PEG-NaCl-Buffer [µL]).
3.1.3. Mix samples gently using the lab rocker, or rock the storage vessels from side to side and incubate at room temperature for 30 seconds.
3.1.4. Repeat the mixing and incubating step.
3.1.5. Place tubes into the magnetic stand and allow the SPRI beads to settle to the magnets.
3.1.6. Remove the clear supernatant.
3.1.7. Be aware that significant bead loss will result in reduced yield.
3.1.8. Add 700 µL 5 M NaCl without removing the tubes from the magnetic stand, incubate for 1 minute, and discard the supernatant.
3.1.9. Repeat the previous washing step.
3.1.10. Remove the tubes from the magnetic stand and add ≥ 20-70 µL of nuclease-free water (or standard buffer like Tris or TE).
3.1.11. Carefully resuspend the beads by slowly mixing them on the lab rocker or by pipetting ten times using wide-pore pipettes until homogeneous.
3.1.12. Incubate at room temperature for 1 minute.
3.1.13. Place the tubes on a magnetic stand, allowing the SPRI beads to settle to the magnets.
3.1.14. If the elution volume is too low so that beads cannot settle to the magnet, flip the magnetic stand while holding the reaction vessels in place.
3.1.15. Transfer the eluate (HMW DNA) into a labelled 1.5 ml DNA LowBind storage vessel.
3.1.16. Combine divided samples.
3.1.17. Check DNA quantity and fragment size.
3.1.18. If DNA fragments are too short, repeat the size selection part using *0.8 SPRIselect and *1.0 PEG-NaCl-Buffer.
4. For long reads (> 1kb) only: PEG-NaCl-Buffer preparation.
4.1. Prepare 20%-PEG-0.75-M-NaCl-Buffer: NaCl 58,44 g/mol: m = M * c * V.
4.1.1. PEG 20%: V% = (v/v)% = volume of solute/volume of solution * 100.
4.1.3. Shake vigorously, vortex and shake again.
5. BUFFER PREPARATION.
5.1. Buffer 1: prepare 1 mL/sample (plus overhang) using liquid stocks.
5.1.1. 100 mM Tris-HCl.
5.1.2. Add 10 mM DTT solution just before use.
5.2. Buffer 2: prepare 500 µL/sample (plus overhang) under the fume hood using liquid stocks.
5.2.1. 1 M Sorbitol.
5.2.2. 25 mM EDTA.
5.2.3. 5.9 mM Citric Acid.
5.2.4. 4.1 mM Sodium Citrate.
5.2.5. 14 mM ß-Mercaptoethanol.
6. SAMPLE PREPARATION.
6.1. If necessary clean lichen material using nuclease-free water and dry the sample.
6.1.1. Cut lichen material into small pieces (µm) using a sterile razor blade or scalpel.
6.1.2. Transfer samples into 2.0 ml Eppendorf Protein LoBind tubes and store them at -80 °C.
6.1.3. Add 400 µL cold acetone (stored at -20 °C ), shake gently and remove the supernatant.
6.1.4. Supernatant can be stored for use in thin-layer chromatography (TLC).
6.1.5. Repeat until supernatant is clear.
6.1.6. Put the tubes in a heating block set at 30 °C under the fume hood until the samples are dry.

input: To perform whole animal fixation via transcardial perfusion for downstream tissue analysis. Available materials: 4% formaldehyde, 0.9% Hep-saline, bottles & pump, surgical tools (scissors, clamps, bone rongeurs, spatula), vials, timer. How to prepare, anesthetize, perfuse, and process the animal?
output: 1. Preparation.
1.1 List Materials Needed for Perfusion.
1.1.1 4% formaldehyde stock solution.
1.1.2 0.9% Hep-saline.
1.1.3 Bottles and perfusion pump.
1.1.4 Surgical tools (scissors, clamps, bone rongeurs, spatula).
1.1.5 Vials for sample storage.
1.1.6 Timer for tracking processing times.
1.2 Prepare Perfusion System.
1.2.1 Switch waste flow to chemical waste bucket.
1.2.2 Prepare perfusion pumps with 0.9% saline and 4% paraformaldehyde.
1.2.3 Check pump flow rate and ensure no air bubbles in system.
2. Anesthesia.
2.1 Inject chlorohydrate 35% into left lower ventral abdomen.
2.2 Wait approximately 5 minutes for anesthetic to take effect.
2.3 Test for reaction by pinching tail tip forcefully.
2.4 Administer additional anesthesia if necessary.
3. Perfusion Process.
3.1 Initiate prefixative rinse with 0.9% saline.
3.1.1 Run saline at max 90 RPM (~24mls/min).
3.1.2 Continue rinse for 3 minutes.
3.2 Transition to formaldehyde perfusion.
3.2.1 Circulate 4% paraformaldehyde at max 90 RPM (~24mls/min).
3.2.2 Maintain formaldehyde flow for 5 minutes.
3.3 Adjust perfusion rate for tissue fixation.
3.3.1 Reduce pump speed to 65 RPM (~16mls/min).
3.3.2 Continue formaldehyde perfusion for 15 minutes.
4. Surgery and Fixation.
4.1 Position animal on downdraft workbench.
4.1.1 Create V-shaped incision above genital area.
4.1.2 Expose abdominal cavity and diaphragm.
4.1.3 Open rib cage to access thoracic cavity.
4.2 Access heart and aorta.
4.2.1 Clamp excess tissue for better access.
4.2.2 Insert catheter needle into aorta via left ventricle.
4.3 Confirm circulation.
4.3.1 Circulate 0.9% saline until limbs discolor.
4.3.2 Switch to 4% paraformaldehyde (250 ml) until neck stiffens.
5. Brain Removal and Processing.
5.1 Expose cranial cavity.
5.1.1 Cut connective tissue under skin.
5.1.2 Expose skull bone using scalpel and bone cutter.
5.2 Extract brain.
5.2.1 Lift occipital, parietal, and frontal bones.
5.2.2 Remove brain from skull; cut optical nerves.
5.3 Fixative Treatment.
5.3.1 Store brain in 4% fixative for 24 hours.
5.4 Sucrose Treatment.
5.4.1 Transfer brain to 20% sucrose solution.
5.4.2 Continue treatment in 30% sucrose solution.
5.4.3 Freeze brains in dry ice prior to cutting.

input: The objective is to quantify multiple cytokines and chemokines using the Luminex Milliplex 9-plex MAG. Have prepared samples and reagents, antibody-immobilized beads, and standards. Now, how to perform the immunobead assay?

1.2. Reconstitute Quality Control 1 and Quality Control 2 with 250 μL deionized water, mix by inverting and vortexing, and store unused portions at -20°C for up to one month.
1.3. Dilute 30 mL of 10X Wash Buffer with 270 mL deionized water and store unused portions at 2-8°C for up to one month.
1.4. Reconstitute Serum Matrix by adding 1.0 mL Assay Buffer to the lyophilized matrix, mix well, and store unused portions at -20°C for up to one month.
2. Immunobead Preparation.
2.1. Sonicate each antibody-bead vial for 30 seconds and vortex for 1 minute.
2.2. Add 150 μL from each antibody bead vial to the Mixing Bottle, bring the final volume to 3.0 mL with Bead Diluent, and vortex well.
2.3. Unused portions of mixed beads may be stored at 2-8°C for up to one month.
3. Working Standards Preparation.
3.1. Reconstitute the Human Metabolic Hormone Panel Standard with 250 μL deionized water, mix by inverting and vortexing, and store unused portions at -20°C for up to one month.
3.2. Prepare serial dilutions by adding 100 μL of each standard to the next tube, resulting in concentrations ranging from 0 to 31,2354 pg/mL.
4. Immunobead Assay.
4.1. Allow all reagents to warm to room temperature (20-25°C) before use.
4.2. Prewet the MAG Plate by pipetting 200 μL of Assay Buffer into each well, seal, and mix on a plate shaker for 10 minutes at room temperature.
4.3. Decant Assay Buffer and remove residual amounts by inverting the plate onto absorbent towels.
4.4. Add 25 μL of each Standard or Control into the appropriate wells, along with 25 μL Assay Buffer to the 0 pg/mL standard.
4.5. Add 25 μL of Serum Matrix solution to the background, standards, and control wells, and 25 μL of Sample to the appropriate wells.
4.6. Vortex the Mixing Bottle and add 25 μL of mixed Beads to each well, shaking intermittently to avoid settling.
4.7. Seal the plate, cover with a lid, wrap with a rubber band, and incubate with agitation on a plate shaker overnight (16-18 hours) at 4°C.
4.8. Gently remove fluid by aspiration and wash the plate 3 times with 200 μL/well of Wash Buffer.
4.9. Add 50 μL of Detection Antibodies to each well, seal, cover, and incubate with agitation on a plate shaker for 30 minutes at room temperature.
4.10. Add 50 μL Streptavidin-Phycoerythrin to each well and incubate with agitation for another 30 minutes at room temperature.
4.11. Gently remove all contents by aspiration and wash the plate 3 times with Wash Buffer.
4.12. Add 100 μL of Sheath Fluid to all wells and resuspend the beads on a plate shaker for 5 minutes.
5. Data Analysis.
5.1. Run the plate on the Luminex 100™ IS and save the data using Bio-Plex Manager software.
5.2. Analyze the data with the software, ensuring events are set to 50 per bead region and sample size is 50 μL.

input: The goal is to generate lentiviruses for neuronal transdifferentiation. Have prepared HEK293T cells to 80% confluence, DNA and Lipofectamine dilutions complete. Now, how to transfect HEK293T cells and collect viral particles?

input: To study fungal diversity in marine sediments, particularly in deep-sea environments, using Illumina metabarcoding. Available materials: sterile syringes, sucrose buffer, DNA extraction kit, NanoDrop spectrophotometer, Qubit 3.0, PCR reagents, Illumina sequencing kit. How to prepare samples, extract DNA, perform PCR, and sequence?
output: 1. Preparation of Syringes.
1.1. Open a sterile syringe package by the end where the syringe tip is located, avoiding movement of the plunger.
1.2. Attach a new scalpel blade to the handle and flame sterilize it using a gas burner.
1.3. Cut and remove the tip of the syringe carefully.
1.4. Close the syringe package and secure it with adhesive tape after the tip is removed.
1.5. Sterilize the scalpel blade again before cutting a new tip.
2. Sampling Tubes Preparation.
2.1. Open the tubes containing sterile sucrose buffer near a gas burner.
2.2. Pipette 5 mL of sterile sucrose buffer into each 15 mL tube.
2.3. Cover each tube with a piece of parafilm to prevent buffer leaks.
2.4. Ensure all tubes contain 25% w/v sucrose buffer, stored at room temperature.
3. Sediment Sampling.
3.1. Make a reference mark on the core to split it into two halves.
3.2. Open five pre-cut 10 mL syringes and pull the plunger back.
3.3. Immerse the syringe cylinders into one half of the core to collect the sample.
3.4. Remove the syringes and transfer the first 5 mL of sediment (10 cm depth) into one 15 mL tube and the remaining 5 mL (5 cm depth) into another tube.
3.5. Shake the tubes to mix the buffer and sediment evenly.
3.6. Seal the tubes with screw caps and wrap them with parafilm.
3.7. Store the tubes in Ziploc-type bags at -20°C during the campaign and transport to the laboratory.
4. Sample Preparation.
4.1. Thaw the samples on ice.
4.2. Centrifuge the samples at maximum velocity for 1 minute at room temperature.
4.3. Discard the supernatant to remove the sucrose buffer. Store the samples at -80°C until further processing.
5. Lyophilization.
5.1. Place the sample tubes uncapped on ice and cover the top with parafilm.
5.2. Make a few holes in the parafilm using a sterile needle.
5.3. Place the samples in the lyophilizer.
5.4. Check the samples after 48 hours using a sterile needle. The sample is ready if the sediment is completely dry.
5.5. Cap the tubes and store the lyophilized samples at -80°C until processing.
6. DNA Extraction.

6.1. Prepare the PCR chamber station by cleaning the entire chamber, including the glass walls. Lay out all materials needed for DNA extraction inside the chamber. Close the chamber and turn on the UV light for 15 minutes. Once ready, turn on the white light and air circulator.
6.2. Weigh 0.15 grams of lyophilized sample and transfer it into a PowerBead tube, taking care to prevent contamination.
6.3. Return the remaining lyophilized samples to -80°C.
6.4. Add 60 µL of C1 solution to the sample.
6.5. Add 100 µL of phenol chloroform in a chemical fume hood.
6.6. Incubate the samples at room temperature for 2 minutes.
6.7. Lay the samples horizontally in the vortex adapter and vortex for 30 seconds without exceeding this time.
6.8. Centrifuge the samples for 1 minute.
6.9. Transfer the supernatant to a sterile 2 mL tube.
6.10. Add 250 µL of C2 solution and vortex for 5 seconds. Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
6.11. Centrifuge the samples for 2 minutes.
6.12. Transfer 600 µL of the supernatant to a sterile 2 mL tube.
6.13. Add 200 µL of C3 solution and vortex for 5 seconds. Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
6.14. Centrifuge the samples for 3 minutes.
6.15. Transfer up to 850 µL of the supernatant to a sterile 2 mL tube.
6.16. Add 650 µL of C4 solution and 450 µL of absolute ethanol. Vortex for 5 seconds.
6.17. Load up to 500 µL onto a column tube. Centrifuge for 30 seconds and discard the flow through.
6.18. Repeat step 18 until the complete sample has been processed.
6.19. Centrifuge the samples for 2 minutes and carefully transfer the column to a new sterile 2 mL tube.
6.20. Add 600 µL of absolute ethanol and centrifuge for 30 seconds. Discard the flow through.
6.21. Centrifuge the samples for 3 minutes and discard the flow through.
6.22. Add 650 µL of C5 solution and centrifuge for 30 seconds. Discard the flow through.
6.23. Centrifuge the samples for 4 minutes and carefully transfer the column to a new sterile 2 mL tube.
6.24. Add 50 µL of C6 solution and incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes.
6.25. Centrifuge for 1.5 minutes.
6.26. Add another 50 µL of C6 solution and incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes.
6.27. Centrifuge for 2 minutes.
6.28. Discard the column.
6.29. Visualize the extracted DNA by running an electrophoresis on a 1% agarose gel using 5 µL of DNA for each sample.
7. Measuring Genomic DNA with a NanoDropTM Lite Spectrophotometer.
7.1. Turn on the NanoDrop and select the DNA option, then choose dsDNA (double-stranded DNA).
7.2. Carefully lift the upper pedestal.
7.3. Clean the upper and lower pedestals by pipetting 2 µL of sterile HPLC grade water onto the bottom pedestal, lower the upper pedestal, and wait for 2 minutes. Clean with Kimwipes.
7.4. Establish a blank by pipetting 1 µL of blank solution onto the bottom pedestal, lower the arm, and press 'Blank'.
7.5. Once the measurement is complete, rinse the arm and clean the pedestals with Kimwipes.
7.6. Repeat step 7.4 to confirm the blank.
7.7. Measure the sample by pipetting 1 µL of DNA into the lower pedestal, lower the upper pedestal, and press 'Measure'. The results will display on the screen.
7.8. After all samples are measured, repeat step 7.3.
8. Measuring Genomic DNA with Qubit 3.0.
8.1. Prepare the working solution by diluting Qubit BR Reagent (Component A) 1:200 in Qubit BR buffer (Component B) in a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube. Ensure each tube has 200 µL.
8.2. Prepare standards by adding 10 µL of standard to 190 µL of working solution. Standard 1: 0 ng/µL, Standard 2: 10 ng/µL.
8.3. Prepare samples by adding 3 µL of DNA to 197 µL of working solution.
8.4. Mix samples and standards by vortexing for 2-3 seconds and spin briefly.
8.5. Incubate all tubes at room temperature for 2 minutes. Perform measurements as instructed in the Qubit 3.0 manual.
9. Fungal PCR and Library Preparation.

9.1. Prepare the PCR chamber station by cleaning the chamber, including the glass walls. Lay out all materials needed for PCR reactions inside the chamber. Close the chamber and turn on the UV light for 15 minutes. Once ready, turn on the white light and air circulator.
9.2. Keep genomic DNA on ice and adjust the DNA concentration to 2 ng/µL.
9.3. Prepare a master mix by multiplying the volume of each PCR reagent by the number of samples and add 10% extra for pipetting errors.
9.4. Run 5 µL of PCR product on a 2% agarose gel to check amplification.
10. Purification of PCR Product.

10.1. Prepare the PCR chamber station by cleaning the chamber and laying out all materials needed for purification. Close the chamber and turn on the UV light for 15 minutes. Once ready, turn on the white light and air circulator.
10.2. Add 96 mL of 100% ethanol to Washing Buffer II (WB2) and mix well, marking the bottle.
10.3. Add 100 µL of Binding Buffer (KB5) and 400 µL of isopropanol to a 1.5 mL microtube, mixing well.
10.4. Add 37 µL of working Binding Buffer to each well, mixing by pipetting up and down 10 times.
10.5. Cover the plate with a clean adhesive cover.
10.6. Spin the plate for 10 minutes at 2250 x g at room temperature.
10.7. Remove the plate cover and quickly flip it over a waste container, shaking briskly to remove all solution.
10.8. Add 150 µL of washing buffer II to each well, mixing by pipetting up and down twice, and wait for 30 seconds.
10.9. Repeat steps 10.7 and 10.8.
10.10. Blot dry the plate on a clean absorbent paper 3-4 times gently.
10.11. Air dry for 10 minutes.
10.12. Add 20 µL of elution buffer to each well, cover with adhesive cover, and vortex for 30 seconds. Centrifuge for 30 seconds to collect the liquid.
10.13. Load 5 µL onto a 1% agarose gel.
11. Illumina Sequencing.
11.1. Use the MiSeq Reagent Kit v3 (600-cycle) to obtain 300 bp for each forward and reverse end.

system_prompt: As a Cell Biology & Culture expert specializing in in vitro mechanical damage models of isolated myofibers, structure the protocol into hierarchical operational steps with parameter inheritance. Ensure reagent continuity across steps. Exclude theoretical explanations.
instruction: Structure the protocol into hierarchical operational steps. Use imperative verbs and ensure reagent continuity. Format steps as: [MainStep] [SubStep] [SubSubStep] with numeric identifiers.
input: To study satellite cell activation by establishing an in vitro mechanical damage model of isolated myofibers. Available materials: glass Pasteur pipettes, 0.2% type I collagenase, 5% BSA solution, DMEM with 1% PS. How to prepare, isolate, damage, and analyze myofibers?
output: 1. Preparation before Dissection.   1.1 Prepare Materials Needed for Dissection.     1.1.1 Prepare glass Pasteur pipettes by inscribing circles with a diamond pen.     1.1.2 Prepare pipette openings with diameters of 1mm (small) or 5mm (large).     1.1.3 Heat-polish the cut ends of the Pasteur pipettes with a burner.     1.1.4 Fit heat-polished pipettes with rubber bulbs.   1.2 Prepare Disaggregation Medium.     1.2.1 Prepare 1mL of 0.2% type I collagenase solution in DMEM containing 1% PS per EDL muscle.     1.2.2 Sterilize the collagenase solution using a 0.45um syringe filter.     1.2.3 Place the collagenase solution in a CO2 incubator at 37°C.   1.3 Prepare 5% BSA Solution.     1.3.1 Sterilize the BSA solution using a 0.45um syringe filter.     1.3.2 Inactivate the BSA solution at 60°C for 30 minutes.     1.3.3 Rinse the surface of all materials with 5% BSA solution.   1.4 Prepare DMEM containing 1% PS for culture and washing.   1.5 Prepare deep Petri dishes with 6-8 mL of DMEM and place in CO2 incubator.   1.6 Prepare slide glasses with pap-pen for immunostaining. 2. Digestion of EDL Muscle Bundle.   2.1 Sacrifice 8-weeks-old C57BL/6 mice using cervical dislocation.   2.2 Spray hindlimbs with 70% ethanol and remove skin.   2.3 Pin forelimbs on a dissection board and cut distal tendons of EDL and TA muscles.   2.4 Pull tendons toward the proximal direction.   2.5 Remove TA muscle.   2.6 Expose EDL muscle by removing connective tissues.   2.7 Cut proximal tendon of EDL muscle using a scalpel.   2.8 Place EDL muscle into Bijou container with prewarmed digestion medium and incubate for 1.5h. 3. Washing and Collection of Individual Myofibers.   3.1 Place digested EDL muscles into Petri dish with washing medium.   3.2 Dissociate muscle into individual myofibers using a large Pasteur pipette.   3.3 Triturate bundles 2-3 times using a small Pasteur pipette.   3.4 Remove debris by washing.   3.5 Place myofibers in DMEM for 3h at 37°C. 4. Co-culture of Intact Myofibers with Damaged Myofibers.   4.1 Add DMEM to each well of a 6-well plate pre-coated with 5% BSA.   4.2 Transfer 150 intact myofibers per well using a small Pasteur pipette.   4.3 Aspirate DMEM and add fresh DMEM.   4.4 Collect 75 myofibers on the right side using a small Pasteur pipette.   4.5 Apply mechanical damage by rolling the edge of a new Pasteur pipette.   4.6 Confirm ratio of intact to damaged myofibers is 1:1 using a microscope.   4.7 Relocate damaged myofibers between intact myofibers by flushing medium. 5. Immunostaining.   5.1 Coat tubes and pipettes with 5% BSA.   5.2 Transfer myofibers into a 1.5mL tube.   5.3 Fix myofibers by adding 2% PFA in PBS.   5.4 Wash three times with washing solution.   5.5 Permeabilize with 0.3% Triton ×100 for 20 minutes.   5.6 Block with 5% goat serum for 20 minutes.   5.7 Incubate with primary antibodies overnight.   5.8 Wash three times.   5.9 Incubate with secondary antibodies for 60 minutes.   5.10 Wash twice with PBS-T and once with PBS.   5.11 Enclose surface with pap-pen and transfer to glass slide.   5.12 Mount cover glass with DAPI medium.   5.13 Stick cover glass and slide with nail polish.   5.14 Image under fluorescence microscope using cellSens software.

system_prompt: As a specialist in Molecular Biology Techniques, provide clear step-by-step instructions for extracting extracellular DNA from sediment using phosphate buffer and NucleoSpin® Soil kit.
instruction: Please describe the protocol in a two-level list format (using 1., 2., 3. numbers, with one-level sub-steps). Include only the steps, not a rationale or materials list. Use concise language and maintain a chronological order.
input: The objective is to extract high-quality extracellular DNA from sediment samples using phosphate buffer and NucleoSpin® Soil kit. Have prepared 2mL tubes, weighed them, and homogenized the sediment. Now, how to proceed with the DNA extraction process?
output: 1. Prepare the sample.
1.1. Annotate 2mL tubes, one per sample, and note their weights.
1.2. Homogenize the sediment using a sterilized spatula and transfer approximately 0.5g of sediment into the tube.
1.3. Add one volume of saturated phosphate buffer (0.12M Na2HPO4; pH ≈ 8) for one volume of sediment.
2. Desorb DNA from mineral and organic particles.
2.1. Attach the 2mL tubes containing sediment and phosphate buffer to an agitator.
2.2. Agitate at slow speed at room temperature for 900 seconds.
3. Precipitate contaminants.
3.1. Centrifuge at 10000rpm for 600 seconds.
3.2. Transfer the supernatant to a new 2mL tube without taking the pellet.
4. Filter lysate.
4.1. Place a NucleoSpin® Inhibitor Removal Column in a collection tube.
4.2. Load up to 650 µL of clear supernatant onto the filter and centrifuge at 11000rpm for 60 seconds.
4.3. Repeat the loading and centrifugation steps until all supernatant is filtered.
4.4. Collect the filtered liquid in a clean tube and discard the column.
5. Adjust binding conditions.
5.1. Add 250 µL of buffer SB to the sample.
5.2. Vortex for 5 seconds and perform a brief centrifugation.
6. Bind DNA.
6.1. Place a NucleoSpin® Soil Column in a collection tube.
6.2. Load 550 µL of the sample onto the column, centrifuge at 11000rpm for 60 seconds, and discard the flow through.
6.3. Load the remaining sample onto the column, centrifuge again, and discard the flow through.
7. Wash and dry the silica membrane.
7.1. Perform four washes using buffers SB, SW1, and SW2, with appropriate volumes and centrifugation steps.
7.2. After each wash, discard the flow through and place the column back into the collection tube.
8. Dry the silica membrane.
8.1. Centrifuge at 11000rpm for 120 seconds.
9. Elute DNA.
9.1. Place the column into a new microcentrifuge tube and add 30 µL of buffer SE.
9.2. Optional: Heat buffer SE at 50°C, then incubate at room temperature for 90 seconds.
9.3. Centrifuge at 11000rpm for 30 seconds, discard the column, and keep the tube containing DNA.
10. Precipitate contaminants.
10.1. Add 150 µL of buffer SL3 and vortex for 5 seconds.
10.2. Incubate at 4°C for 300 seconds and centrifuge at 11000rpm for 60 seconds.

system_prompt: As an expert in cell biology and culture protocols, specializing in mitochondrial respiration assays and extracellular flux analysis, structure the protocol into hierarchical operational steps with parameter inheritance. instruction: Reconstruct the protocol into a hierarchical structure with multi-level steps (main steps, sub-steps, sub-sub-steps). Use imperative verbs, maintain consistent tense, and ensure reagent continuity. Exclude theoretical explanations. Format steps as: [MainStep] [SubStep] [SubSubStep] with numeric identifiers.
input: To measure respiratory activity in permeabilized cells using extracellular flux analysis. Available materials: XF Cell Microplate, T75 culture dish, sterile PBS, trypsin-EDTA, cell culture growth medium, hemocytometer, DMEM with FBS and penicillin-streptomycin, XF24 FluxPak, MAS buffer, FA-free BSA, cell lysis buffer. How to prepare cells, synchronize them, hydrate the FluxPak, set up the XF24 experiment, and analyze the data?
output: 1. Seeding the Cells in the XF Cell Microplate.   1.1. Cell Growth and Preparation.     1.1.1. Grow the cells in a T75 culture dish to achieve the desired amount of cells.     1.1.2. Rinse the cells once with 10 ml of sterile PBS (pH 7.4, kept at RT) before trypsinization.   1.2. Trypsinization and Cell Suspension.     1.2.1. Add 2–5 ml of trypsin-EDTA solution to the flask and swirl it to make sure that the cells are covered with trypsin solution.     1.2.2. Place the flask in the incubator (5% CO2) for 3 min at 37 °C.     1.2.3. Add 8 ml of cell culture growth medium to the cell mixture (warmed to 37 °C in the water bath).   1.3. Centrifugation and Cell Resuspension.     1.3.1. Transfer the cell suspension to a 15-ml conical tube and centrifuge it at 300–500g for 5 min at RT.     1.3.2. Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 1–3 ml of cell culture growth medium.   1.4. Cell Counting and Seeding.     1.4.1. Count the cells with a hemocytometer and adjust the concentration of counted cells to ten times the desired cell number to be seeded in each well.     1.4.2. Seed the cells into the XF24 culture plate by pipetting 100 μl of the cell suspension into each well. 2. Synchronizing Cells (Optional).   2.1. On the next day, carefully aspirate each well and replace the medium with prewarmed DMEM (containing 0–0.5% (vol/vol) FBS and 1% (vol/vol) penicillin-streptomycin).   2.2. Incubate the plate for 24 h to synchronize the cell cycle of dividing cells. 3. Rehydrating an XF24 FluxPak.   3.1. Hydrate the cartridge by adding ∼1 ml of XF calibrant solution into each well of the utility plate.   3.2. Place the cartridge back onto the utility microplate and incubate the plate in a non-CO2 incubator at 37 °C. 4. Setting up the XF24 Experiment Protocol.   4.1. Preparing the MAS-BSA Solution.     4.1.1. Weigh 200 mg of FA–free BSA and add it to 50 ml of MAS buffer (yielding a 4 mg ml−1 MAS-BSA solution).     4.1.2. Warm the MAS-BSA solution to 37 °C in the water bath and adjust the pH to 7.2 with KOH or HCl if needed.   4.2. Preparing Injection Solutions.     4.2.1. Pipette ∼15 ml of the warmed MAS-BSA solution into a clean conical tube, and use it to make 10× stock concentrations of the compounds to be loaded into the ports of the reagent delivery cartridges.     4.2.2. Load 10× solutions into their respective ports.   4.3. Calibrating the Cartridge.     4.3.1. Insert the hydrated XF cartridge into the XF analyzer and hit 'start' to run the calibration step.     4.3.2. Wait for the calibration to complete. 5. Replacing the Medium with MAS-BSA Buffer.   5.1. Remove the XF culture plate from the incubator and gently aspirate all but 50 μl of DMEM culture medium.   5.2. Gently add 700 μl of warmed MAS-BSA buffer to each well.   5.3. Aspirate all but 50 μl of the buffer from each well and add 625 μl of MAS-BSA buffer to each well. 6. Running the XF Assay.   6.1. Place the cells in a non-CO2 incubator until the calibration is complete.   6.2. After the cartridge has been calibrated, hit 'ok', remove the calibrant plate and discard it.   6.3. Place the XF cell culture plate on the platform, and hit 'continue' to run the remainder of the experimental protocol. 7. Determining Protein Concentration and Normalizing Data.   7.1. Quickly but carefully aspirate and discard the solution from each well.   7.2. Add 1 ml of PBS (at RT) to each well, and then aspirate and discard the solution from each well.   7.3. Repeat the washing step once more.   7.4. Add 20 μl of cell lysis buffer to each well and follow the steps for protein concentration estimation and data normalization. 8. Calculations and Data Analysis.   8.1. Calculate state 3, state 4o and RCR values using the points indicated on the sample data set.   8.2. Use permeabilized cells not provided with substrate as controls and measures of state 1 respiration.

Place the eyeball on a white Whatman filter paper under dim red illumination.   3.2. Pierce through the cornea with a razor blade.   3.2.1. Orientation and Isolation of Retina.   4.1. Mark the dorsal orientation by making a small cut at the peripheral retina.   4.2.1. Isolate the retina from the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) using forceps.   4.2.2. Cut the retina into dorsal and ventral halves along the nasal-temporal axis. 5. Mounting of Retina.   5.1. Mount the retina with the ganglion cell layer facing up onto the precut filter paper.   5.2. Keep the mounted retina in the oxygenated incubation chamber with Ames' medium in darkness at room temperature. 6. Two-Photon Targeted Recording of GFP-Expressing Neurons.   6.1. Switch back to infrared optics and the CCD camera to visualize the target cell body at the reference point.   6.3.4. Use an empty patch electrode to dissect the inner limiting membrane to expose the target cell.   6.4.1. Fill a new electrode with internal solution and perform loose patch, cell-attached, or whole-cell recordings.   6.4.2. (Optional) Add Alexa Fluor 594 to the pipette solution to verify targeting with a two-photon confocal image. 7. Recording Light Responses from the GFP-Expressing Neuron.   7.1. (Optional) Switch to the objective used for light stimulation if different from the recording objective.   7.2. Focus the objective onto the photoreceptor layer.   7.3. Switch to the correct filter position for light stimulation and turn off all light sources except the OLED screen.   7.4. Allow the retina to adapt to background light intensity before presenting visual stimuli.   7.5. Present light stimuli and record the cell's light response.   7.6. input: To quantify and assess the integrity of genomic DNA isolated from bacterial cultures using IMPLEN nano spectrophotometer, Qubit fluorometer, and Agilent TapeStation. How to quantify DNA concentration, assess purity, and evaluate size distribution?
output: 1. Quantification of DNA with the IMPLEN Nano Spectrophotometer.
1.1. Turn on the Implen and select "Nucleic Acids." Ensure the arm is down during initialization.
1.2. Measure the blank: Pipet 2 µL of sample buffer onto the sample window. Lower the arm and click "Blank."
1.3. Measure the sample: Pipet 2 µL of genomic DNA onto the sample window. Lower the arm and click "Sample."
1.4. Record the concentration (ng/µL) and A260/A280 ratio.
1.5. Clean the sample window and top sensor with a Kimwipe. If necessary, use water to thoroughly clean the pedestal and mirror.
2. DNA Quantification with Qubit.
2.1. Label 3 tubes: "1" (Standard 1), "2" (Standard 2), and the bacterial species number (e.g., "105" for the sample).
2.2. Prepare standards: Add 10 µL of each Qubit standard to 190 µL of working solution in separate tubes. Final volume: 200 µL.
2.3. Prepare samples: Add 2 µL of genomic DNA to 198 µL of working solution in separate tubes. Final volume: 200 µL.
2.4. Mix samples by vortexing for 5 seconds.
2.5. Incubate all tubes at room temperature for 120 seconds.
2.6. Calibrate the Qubit fluorometer using standards. Insert Standard #1, press "Run Standards," then insert Standard #2, press "Run Standards" again.
2.7. Measure samples. Enter the sample volume (2 µL) in the software. Insert sample tubes and press "Run Sample."
2.8. Record DNA concentrations (ng/µL) in notes and on sample tubes.
3. Genomic DNA Assessment with TapeStation.
3.1. Equilibrate genomic DNA reagents at room temperature for 1800 seconds.
3.2. Flick the Genomic DNA ScreenTape and insert into the TapeStation nest.
3.3. Vortex reagents and samples. Spin down before use.
3.4. Prepare ladder: Pipet 10 µL of sample buffer and 1 µL of genomic DNA ladder into a tube strip.
3.5. For each sample, pipet 10 µL of sample buffer and 1 µL of genomic DNA into separate tube strips.
3.6. Apply caps to tube strips.
3.7. Mix samples using an IKA MS3 vortexer at 2000 rpm for 60 seconds.
3.8. Spin down samples and ladder for 60 seconds.
3.9. Load samples into the TapeStation. Place ladder in position A1 on the tube strip holder.
3.10. Remove caps of tube strips. Visually confirm liquid position. Click "Start."
3.11. Analyze results using TapeStation software.

input: The objective is to measure non-esterified fatty acids (NEFA) in serum and plasma using a 96-well kit. Prepared samples, standards, and reagents. Now, how to perform the NEFA measurement?

1.2. Add dilution buffer to each well to reach a total sample volume of 50 μl.

5.3. Gently shake the plate to ensure thorough mixing.
6. Final incubation and equilibration.
6.1. Place in a 37ºC incubator for 10 minutes.
6.2. Allow the plate to equilibrate to room temperature for 5 minutes.
6.3. During this time, ensure that there are no bubbles in the solution mixture.
6.4. Use a large gauge needle or clean pipet tip to pop any bubbles as this will result in inaccurate absorbance readings.

input: To study host-pathogen interactions using zebrafish embryos. Available materials: E. coli-GFP bacteria, tryptic soy broth (TSB), agar, ampicillin, methylene blue, PTU, phenol red, PBS, benzocaine. How to prepare embryos, cultivate bacteria, perform microinjection, and analyze infection dynamics?
output: 1. Preparing the Embryos.   1.1 Transfer adult zebrafish to a 3L breeding tank in the evening.   1.2 Collect embryos using a mesh strainer and transfer to a 10 cm Petri dish with 25ml E3 media and 0.3mg/L methylene blue.   1.3 Remove dead or unfertilized eggs and transfer remaining embryos to an incubator at 28°C.   1.4 At 24 hpf, transfer embryos to E3 media with 0.3mg/L methylene blue and 0.003% PTU.   1.5 Replace E3 media daily until 72 hpf.   1.6 Dissect embryos unhatched by 72 hpf using watchmaker's forceps. 2. Tryptic Soy Broth Preparation.   2.1 Weigh 15g TSB powder and transfer to 1L glass bottle.   2.2 Add 500ml Milli-Q water and magnetic stir bar.   2.3 Autoclave at 121°C, 400-500 kPa for 1 hour 30 minutes.   2.4 Allow media to cool at room temperature before storing at 4°C. 3. Tryptic Soy-Agar-Ampicillin Plate Preparation.   3.1 Weigh 6g agar and 15g TSB powder to 1L glass bottle.   3.2 Add 500ml Milli-Q water and magnetic stir bar.   3.3 Autoclave at 121°C for 1 hour 30 minutes.   3.4 Allow media to cool and add 500μl ampicillin solution (100mg/ml).   3.5 Pour 25ml TSB-agar-ampicillin solution into 10 cm Petri dishes.   3.6 Close Petri dish lid, seal with parafilm, and store at 4°C. 4. Bacterial Cultivation and Enumeration.   4.1 Inoculate E. coli-GFP bacteria into 10ml TSB with 10μl ampicillin.   4.2 Grow bacterial culture overnight at 37°C in a shaking incubator.   4.3 Determine Colony Forming Units (CFU).     4.3.1 Transfer 1ml bacterial culture to a cuvette.     4.3.2 Use spectrophotometer to measure absorbance at 600nm.   4.4 Perform serial dilutions of bacterial culture (10^-6 to 10^-10).   4.5 Plate 50-100μl diluted broth onto TSB-agar-ampicillin plates and incubate overnight at 37°C.   4.6 Pellet bacterial cells at 13,751xg for 1-2 minutes and remove supernatant.   4.7 Resuspend bacterial cells in sterile PBS at 9×10^10 CFU/ml. 5. Microinjection of Bacterial Cells into Embryos.   5.1 Form a precision glass capillary tube into a fine needle using a micropipette puller.   5.2 Place needle on a square plate with Blu-tack for protection.   5.3 Prepare injection material by mixing 4μl 9×10^10 CFU bacteria-PBS suspension with 1μl 2% phenol red.   5.4 Load needle with 3μl injection material using a microloader pipette.   5.5 Shake needle to bring injection material to the tip and remove air bubbles.   5.6 Secure needle in microinjector housing and adjust micromanipulator position.   5.7 Anesthetize 72 hpf embryos with 0.1mg/ml benzocaine in E3 media.   5.8 Inject 2-5 nl of solution into the venous return of each embryo.   5.9 Transfer embryos to fresh E3 media with methylene blue and PTU for recovery.   5.10 Include 30-60 embryos per experimental group, with sterile PBS injected and uninjected controls.   5.11 Remove dead or deformed embryos and homogenize 5 injected embryos for CFU determination. 6. Imaging of Injected Embryos.   6.1 Transfer embryos to 12-well or 6-well plates.   6.2 Anesthetize embryos with E3 media containing 0.1mg/ml benzocaine.   6.3 Orient embryos for imaging and repeat at 0, 4, 8, 16, 24, and 48 hpi. 7. Bacterial Enumeration by Plate Counting.   7.1 Collect 10 live injected larvae at each time point in Eppendorf tubes.   7.2 Rinse once in fresh E3 media to remove benzocaine.   7.3 Transfer 1,000μl 1% Triton X-100 in sterile PBS to the tube.   7.4 Homogenize samples in a Qiagen tissue lyser II for 5 minutes.   7.5 Plate 50-100μl homogenate onto TSB-agar-ampicillin plates and incubate at 37°C for up to 48 hours.   7.6 Confirm E. coli-GFP growth under fluorescence microscopy.

system_prompt: As an expert in cancer metastasis research specializing in in vivo cancer cell extravasation quantification using the chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) of chicken embryos, structure the protocol into multi-level steps with parameter inheritance and logical flow.
instruction: Decompose the protocol into hierarchical operational steps (MainStep.SubStep.SubSubStep) with imperative verbs, maintain parameter continuity, and exclude theoretical explanations. Ensure steps are numbered and include precise parameters.
input: To quantify cancer cell extravasation in vivo using the CAM of chicken embryos. Available materials: fertilized eggs, Dremel tool, Dulbecco's PBS (D-PBS),Trypsin, EDTA, CellTracker dye, lectin-rhodamine, microinjector, wide-field fluorescence microscope, confocal microscope. How to prepare embryos, process cancer cells, inject into CAM veins, and analyze extravasation efficiency?
output: 1. Preparation of Ex Ovo Chicken Embryos.   1.1 Incubation of Fertilized Eggs.     1.1.1 Place the eggs in the hatcher and incubate them for 4 d at 39 °C with >70% relative humidity and rotation.     1.1.2 If delayed, store eggs at 4 °C for up to 3 d, then move to 22 °C for 3 h before incubation at 39 °C.   1.2 Preparation of Dremel Tool.     1.2.1 Fit a cutting disc (no. 36, 15/16-inch diameter) to a rod platform with a three-finger clamp.     1.2.2 Spray the Dremel tool and disc with 70% ethanol.   1.3 Cracking Open the Egg Shell.     1.3.1 Place the egg on its side for 10 s and roll the middle 'waist' with 70% ethanol.     1.3.2 Use the Dremel tool at medium speed to make four shallow cuts around the middle 'waist'.     1.3.3 Spray a new weigh boat with 70% ethanol and gently roll the egg back and forth while applying downward pressure.   1.4 Removal of Egg Shell and Transfer of Embryo.     1.4.1 Crack open the shell and lay the yolk and embryo in the weigh boat.     1.4.2 Discard unfertilized eggs and reuse weigh boats for other embryos.   1.5 Placement of Embryo in Petri Dish.     1.5.1 Cover the weigh boat with a transparent square plastic Petri dish.     1.5.2 Repeat for additional eggs as needed.   1.6 Storage and Transport of Embryos.     1.6.1 Place embryos in larger containers and store in an egg incubator at 39 °C with >70% relative humidity and no rocking. 2. Preparation of Cancer Cells for Injection.   2.1 Washing of Cells.     2.1.1 Discard medium into a flask with 20% bleach and wash the flask with D-PBS three times.   2.2 Trypsinization of Cells.     2.2.1 Add 2 ml of 0.05% Trypsin with 0.053 mM EDTA to the flask.     2.2.2 Ensure even distribution and incubate at 37 °C for 5–8 min.   2.3 Collection and Centrifugation of Cells.     2.3.1 Collect cells and transfer to a sterile 15-ml Falcon tube.     2.3.2 Add additional D-PBS to collect residual cells and centrifuge at 200g for 10 min at 25 °C.   2.4 Resuspension of Cells.     2.4.1 Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 10 ml of D-PBS.     2.4.2 Centrifuge again at 200g for 10 min at 25 °C.   2.5 Final Resuspension and Transfer of Cells.     2.5.1 Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 1.0 ml of D-PBS using a P1000 micropipette.   2.6 Labeling of Cells with CellTracker Dye.     2.6.1 Add 2 μl of diluted CellTracker dye and mix for 10 s.     2.6.2 Leave on ice for 10 min in the dark.   2.7 Washing and Resuspension of Labeled Cells.     2.7.1 Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200g for 10 min at 25 °C.     2.7.2 Remove supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1.0 ml of D-PBS.     2.7.3 Repeat the wash step.   2.8 Dilution of Cells.     2.8.1 Determine cell concentration using a hemocytometer or automated cell counter.     2.8.2 Dilute cells to 5.0 × 10^5 cells per ml with D-PBS.   2.9 Incubation with Inhibitory Antibody, Peptide or Ligand.     2.9.1 Incubate diluted cells with the antibody/peptide/ligand for 15 min in the dark at 25 °C.     2.9.2 Wash cells twice and dilute to the original volume. 3. I.V. Injection of Cancer Cells into CAM Veins.   3.1 Assembly of Microinjector.     3.1.1 Fit an 18-gauge needle onto a 1-ml syringe and insert the needle into a 5–6-inch piece of Tygon tubing.   3.2 Drawing of Cell Suspension into Microinjector.     3.2.1 Draw 400–500 μl of cell suspension into the microinjector.     3.2.2 Expel air from the syringe barrel.   3.3 Injection of Cell Suspension into CAM Veins.     3.3.1 Locate bright red vessels using a dissecting scope with white-light illumination.     3.3.2 Glide the needle along the vein until it catches the CAM, then slowly raise the CAM until a 'bloom' of blood appears.   3.4 Injection of Cell Suspension.     3.4.1 When the 'bloom' is observed, slowly drop the CAM and press the syringe plunger to inject 100 μl of cell suspension.     3.4.2 Ensure clear fluid enters the vessel and flows toward the embryo.   3.5 Removal of Needle and Absorption of Blood.     3.5.1 Remove the needle and use rolled-up Kimwipes to absorb blood and cell suspension from the injection site.   3.6 Application of Foil Windows.     3.6.1 Apply 2–3 foil windows to the CAM surface away from the injection site.     3.6.2 Repeat for each embryo as required. 4. Extravasation Efficiency Data Collection Using Wide-Field Fluorescence Microscopy.   4.1 Counting of Cells at T = 0.     4.1.1 Use a wide-field fluorescence microscope with a 10× objective to count all cells within each foil window immediately after injection.   4.2 Incubation of Embryos.     4.2.1 Place all embryos back in the incubator and incubate for 24 h at 39 °C with >70% relative humidity.   4.3 Analysis of Extravasation Efficiency Data.     4.3.1 Count the number of cells within each foil window at T = 24 h using the wide-field fluorescence microscope.     4.3.2 Record values on the lid of each embryo and ensure correspondence with foil windows.     4.3.3 Divide the number of extravasated cells at T = 24 h by the number of intravascular cells at T = 0 h to calculate mean extravasation efficiency. 5. Confocal Microscopy of Intravascular Versus Extravasated Cells.   5.1 Injection of Lectin-Rhodamine.     5.1.1 Inject 75 μl of diluted lectin-rhodamine using a microinjector.     5.1.2 Wait for 5 min after injection.   5.2 Confocal Microscopy.     5.2.1 Place the embryo in the imaging chamber and position the coverslip over a foil window.     5.2.2 Use a confocal microscope with a 60× objective to detect green and red fluorescence signals.     5.2.3 Determine whether cells are within the red vasculature (lectin-rhodamine) or have extravasated.     5.2.4 Calculate the proportion of cells remaining in the intravascular space.

1.1. Combine 10 mL of 0.2 M copper sulfate solution (or 5.0 g per batch) with 10 mL of 0.1% gelatin solution in water under magnetic stirring.
1.2. Heat the mixture at 70°C for 30 minutes.
2. Add sodium borohydride.
2.1. Slowly introduce 10 mL of 0.4 M sodium borohydride solution (or 0.15 g per batch) into the heated mixture over 5–10 minutes.
3. Adjust pH and reheat.
3.1. Add 6 mL of 1 M sodium hydroxide to adjust the pH from approximately 2 to 12.
3.2. Heat the mixture again at 70°C with magnetic stirring for 30 minutes.
4. Purify the nanoparticles.
4.1. Centrifuge the solution at 8000×g for 30 minutes to collect the nanoparticles.
4.2. Resuspend the pellet in 30 mL of milli-Q water and repeat the precipitation and washing steps two additional times.
5. Final processing and storage.
5.1. Disperse the purified nanoparticles in absolute ethanol and dry at 60°C for 8 hours.
5.2. Transfer the dried nanoparticles into light-protecting containers and store them in a desiccator at room temperature for future use.

input: To isolate vertically-transmitted Symbiodiniaceae from coral eggs using centrifugation. Available materials: bowls, filter mesh, falcon tubes, pipettes, seawater, Eppendorf tubes, liquid nitrogen. How to collect gametes, wash bundles, centrifuge, quantify cells, aliquot, and freeze samples?
output: 1. Collect Coral Gametes.
1.1. Isolate coral colonies at signs of setting.
1.2. Collect gamete bundles using cups and pipettes. Label with coral ID and time of spawning.
2. Wash Gamete Bundles and Prepare Falcon Tubes.
2.1. Separate and wash gamete bundles using bowls and filter mesh. Ensure mesh is finer than egg size.
2.2. Fill bowls with seawater and place filter inside. Ensure mesh side is submerged.
2.3. Pour bundles into filter and agitate to break up. Eggs remain, sperm enter bowl.
2.4. Transfer filter to second bowl, wash eggs. Dispose of sperm water and refresh bowls.
2.5. Continue agitating and transferring until eggs form mono-film. Eggs must be free of sperm for centrifugation.
2.6. Transfer eggs into falcon tubes using pipette. Maintain equal total volume. Use recommended ratios: 15ml tubes (0.8ml eggs to 13ml seawater), 10ml tubes (0.5ml eggs to 8ml seawater).
3. Centrifuge, Remove Supernatant, Resuspend, and Repeat.
3.1. Centrifuge falcon tubes at specified settings. First spin should have maximum force.
3.2. Remove supernatant and lipid layer. Tap tube to dislodge lipid pancake.
3.3. Optional: Combine samples of same genotype. Do not mix with tubes containing lipids.
3.4. Top up tubes with seawater to 10ml and mix. Repeat centrifugation until no lipids remain.
3.5. Remove contact lipids using pipette or scraping. Resuspend pellet in 1ml seawater.
4. Quantify Cell Count for Each Genotype.
4.1. Combine falcon tubes into 250ml flask by genotype. Label as master culture.
4.2. Top up master cultures with seawater to known volume (e.g., 100ml).
4.3. Determine cells per 1ml (CCC) using haemocytometer. Example: CCC = 587,500 cells/ml.
4.4. Calculate required volume for Desired Cell Count (DCC). Example: DCC = 5,000,000 cells. Required volume = DCC / CCC = 8.5ml.
5. Aliquot and Re-pellet into Final Tubes.
5.1. Check if required volume exceeds final tube capacity (1.5ml Eppendorf).
5.2. Centrifuge 1.5ml tubes. Discard supernatant and excess water.
5.3. For volumes exceeding 1.5ml, aliquot into 15ml falcon tubes and centrifuge.
5.4. Discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 1ml seawater.
5.5. Aliquot required volume into 1.5ml LoBind Eppendorf tubes. Label with genotype and cell count.
6. Snap Freeze Samples and Store.
6.1. Snap freeze tubes using liquid nitrogen bath.
6.2. Store samples in -80C freezer for DNA extraction.

input: To reliably isolate and identify commensal E. coli strains from feces of healthy laboratory mice or rats. How to collect fecal samples, perform serial dilution and plating, conduct colony PCR, and sequence the isolates?
output: 1. Fecal Collection.   1.1 Put a healthy NIH Swiss mouse or SD rat into a clean cage and wait for defecation.   1.2 Use sterile forceps to transfer one fresh fecal pellet into a 1.5m centrifuge tube preloaded with 1 ml of 1x PBS.   1.3 Put the tubes with fecal pellet on ice and immediately transfer them back to the lab to perform serial dilution and plating. 2. Serial Dilution and Plating.   2.1 Homogenize the fecal pellet thoroughly by vortexing for 30 sec at maximum speed.   2.2 Add 900ul of 1× PBS into four 1.5m centrifuge tubes and perform 1:10 serial dilution from the fecal samples using wide bore tips.   2.3 Use cell spreaders to plate 100ul of each dilution onto MacConkey agar plates (10^-1 to 10^-5).   2.4 Incubate the plates aerobically at 37°C for 16-18h. 3. Colony PCR for E. coli Identification.   3.1 Select potential E. coli colonies that appear as red and round shaped colonies due to lactose fermentation capability.   3.2 Add 50ul of PCR reaction mix into each PCR tube.   3.3 Use P10 tips to pick a small amount of the single colony and swirl in the PCR reaction.   3.4 Complete the reaction in a thermal cycler following the PCR program.   3.5 Gel Electrophoresis and PCR Clean-up.     3.5.1 Prepare 40ml of 1% agarose gel by dissolving 0.4g agarose in 1x TAE and heating.     3.5.2 Mix 5ul of PCR reaction with 1ul of 6× DNA loading dye and apply the samples along with the marker to the gel.     3.5.3 Run the electrophoresis for 30 min at 100V and take a picture to check amplification using a UV transilluminator.     3.5.4 Perform PCR clean-up using a GeneJET gel extraction and DNA cleanup kit following manufacturer instructions.   3.6 Sequence the cleaned-up samples by Sanger sequencing using 16S rRNA gene primers.   3.7 Search the 16S rRNA gene sequences against the Ribosomal Database Project (RDP) and NCBI nucleotide database.   3.8 Select isolates sharing >98% 16S rRNA sequence identity with E. coli type strain and culture them in LB broth overnight for glycerol stocks. 4. Whole Genome Sequencing and Annotation.   4.1 Culture selected isolates overnight in 5ml LB broth for genomic DNA extraction using PureLink Genomic DNA Mini Kit.   4.2 Perform whole genome sequencing on Illumina MiSeq platform using Nextera XT DNA library preparation kit.   4.3 Quantify library concentrations using Qubit 3.0 fluorometer and normalize to 2nM.   4.4 Denature libraries with 0.1N NaOH and mix with 5% PhiX genomic DNA as positive control.   4.5 Sequence denatured libraries on Illumina MiSeq with 2x300bp reads.   4.6 Genome Assembly and Annotation.     4.6.1 Assemble draft genome using SPAdes assembler.     4.6.2 Evaluate assemblies using Quality Assessment Tool for Genome Assemblies (QUAST).     4.6.3 Map raw reads back to SPAdes contigs using BBMap.     4.6.4 Blast contigs against NBCI reference bacterial genomes using Megablast.     4.6.5 Annotate genome using Rapid Annotations using Subsystems Technology (RAST).   4.7 Predict toxin-related virulence in E. coli isolate's whole genome using IslandViewer.

input: To achieve high-resolution imaging of brain tissue ultrastructure using electron microscopy, while minimizing artifacts and enhancing contrast. Available materials: 150 uL pentobarbital (Euthasol), 50 mL 37°C PBS, 50 mL 37°C 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA), 3% glutaraldehyde, 1% paraformaldehyde, 5% sucrose in 0.1M sodium cacodylate trihydrate. How to perform brain perfusion, sample preparation, and imaging?
output: 1. Brain Perfusion.
1.1. Anesthetize mice with 150 uL pentobarbital (Euthasol).
1.2. Perform heart puncture to start perfusion.
1.3. Perfuse with 50 mL of 37°C PBS at a flow rate of 6 mL/min.
1.4. Follow with 50 mL of 37°C 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) at the same flow rate.
1.5. Dissect brains and place them immediately into cold (4°C) fixative solution containing 3% glutaraldehyde, 1% paraformaldehyde, 5% sucrose in 0.1M sodium cacodylate trihydrate.
2. Sample Preparation.
2.1. Transfer tissue blocks to brass high-pressure freezing planchettes prefilled with buffer containing 10% 70kD Ficoll.
2.2. Place planchettes into a high-pressure freezing machine and ultra-rapidly freeze the tissue.
2.3. Transfer planchettes under liquid nitrogen to cryotubes containing a frozen solution of 2% osmium tetroxide, 0.05% uranyl acetate in acetone.

2.4. Place tubes in a freeze-substitution machine and perform the following steps: maintain at -90°C for 72 hours, warm to -20°C over 24 hours, hold at -20°C for 12 hours, then warm to 4°C over 1 hour.
2.5. Rinse samples 3 times with cold (4°C) acetone and bring to room temperature.
2.6. Infiltrate samples into Epon-Araldite resin using the following schedule: 2:1 (Acetone:Resin) for 1 hour, 1:1 for 1 hour, 1:2 for 1 hour.
2.7. Transfer samples into 100% resin and remove from planchettes.
2.8. Allow samples to infiltrate into resin for 24 hours with gentle agitation.
2.9. Embed brain tissue samples into resin containing accelerator (DMP30) between two Teflon-coated glass microscope slides.
2.10. Polymerize resin for 24-48 hours at 60°C.
2.11. Examine embedded tissue blocks with a dissecting microscope, select optimal regions, and excise with a scalpel.
2.12. Reglue excised samples onto plastic sectioning stubs.
2.13. Cut semi-thin (170 nm) sections using an ultramicrotome, collect onto formvar-coated copper-rhodium 1mm slot grids, and stain with 3% uranyl acetate and lead citrate.
3. Imaging.
3.1. Image grids using a transmission electron microscope equipped with a Gatan US1000 2k x 2k CMOS camera.
3.2. Collect large-area montaged images of brain regions automatically using SerialEM software.
3.3. Align and analyze images using the IMOD software package and AIVIA image analysis software with machine learning algorithms to identify mitochondria.

1.3. Prepare 30 µL sample for loading by adding 20 µg of protein lysate to the required volume of dH2O and 7.5 µL of 4X NuPage LDS sample buffer.
1.4. Perform BCA assay as per manufacturer's protocol to determine protein concentration of lysates.
1.5. Transfer supernatant to new microcentrifuge tubes and discard pellet.
2. Running Gels.
2.1. Thaw samples from freezer on ice and place on heating block for 600 seconds at 70°C.
2.2. Run gel at 180 V (constant voltage) for 3600 seconds at Room temperature.
2.3. Load 4 µL of the ladder and 25 µL of the samples prepared at 1 mg/mL (or as needed).
2.4. After samples have heated, quickly vortex and spin down.
2.5. Place 12-well gel(s) into casket and clip in place. Fill up the centre part with 1 X MES buffer and check for any leaks. Once in place, add 1 X MES to the outer space until half way full.
