3. Transfer and blocking.
3.1. Obtain large container and fill with 1 X transfer buffer.
3.2. Place membrane in container and cover with 5% skim milk in TBS-T solution, place on rocking platform for 3600 seconds.
3.3. Perform transfer at 90 V (constant voltage) for 5400 seconds in cold room.
3.4. Open sandwich apparatus and place components in the following order: sponge, filter paper, gel, nitrocellulose membrane, filter paper, sponge.
3.5. For each gel, obtain a sandwich apparatus, 2 X sponges, 2 X filter paper, 1 X nitrocellulose membrane (0.45 µm).
4. Primary and secondary antibody incubations.
4.1. Prepare primary antibody in 5% skim milk in TBS-T solution (dilution 1:1000).
4.2. Wash blots with TBS-T every 3 times for 600 seconds.
4.3. Incubation at Room temperature for 3600 seconds with gentle rocking.
4.4. Prepare secondary antibody (anti-mouse or anti-rabbit HRP conjugated antibody) in 2.5% skim milk in TBS-T solution.
4.5. Wash blots with TBS-T every 3 times for 600 seconds.
4.6. Incubation at 4°C overnight with gentle rocking.
4.7. Cut blots using scissors into smaller strips as desired.
5. Blot imaging.
5.1. Visualise bands using BioRad ChemiDoc MP Imaging System chemiluminescence mode.
5.2. Band analysis and quantification is performed in ImageLab, all proteins are normalised to B-actin used as a loading control.
6. Stripping and.
6.1. If stripping membrane is required to reprobe with another antibody, add Abcam mild stripping buffer and incubate for 600 seconds at Room temperature with rocking.
6.2. Repeat step 17 onwards with new primary antibody as required.
6.3. Wash membrane 3 times with TBS-T for 600 seconds each, then block in 5% skim milk in TBS-T solution for 3600 seconds.

system_prompt: As a Genomics Technologies protocol expert, provide detailed step-by-step instructions for RNA purification using cellulose-based methods.
instruction: Please describe the protocol in a two-level numbered list (using 1., 2., 3. numbers, with one-level sub-steps) for the purification of IVT mRNA. Include only the operational steps, no explanations or materials list. Ensure the steps are concise, logically ordered, and follow standard experimental protocols.
input: The aim is to purify IVT mRNA using a cellulose-based method as part of the LungMAP initiative's workflow. Have prepared the necessary buffers and calculated the required cellulose. Now, provide the step-by-step procedure for RNA purification.
output: 1. Prepare chromatography buffer.
1.1. Add 40.24 mL nuclease-free water to a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
1.2. Add 0.5 mL HEPES solution (10 mM final concentration).
1.3. Add 10 μL EDTA solution (0.1 mM final concentration).
1.4. Add 1.25 mL NaCl solution (125 mM final concentration).
1.5. Add 8 mL ethanol (200 proof, 16% v/v).
1.6. Invert the tube 6-8 times to mix.
2. Cellulose preparation.
2.1. Calculate the required amount of cellulose: (number of RNA samples to be purified x 2 x 0.2) = grams of cellulose needed.
2.2. Weigh out the calculated amount of cellulose under RNA conditions and add to a 50 mL conical tube.
2.3. Add the calculated volume of chromatography buffer to the cellulose tube.
2.4. Attach the cellulose tube to a vortex platform, shake continuously at notch 2 or 3 for 10 minutes.
2.5. Pipet 700 µL of cellulose slurry to the top of each NucleoSpin column tube.
2.6. Spin NucleoSpin column tubes at 14,000 x g for 60 seconds at room temperature.
2.7. Discard the flowthrough and add 500 µL chromatography buffer to each NucleoSpin column tube.
2.8. Attach the tubes to the vortex platform, shake vigorously for 5 minutes.
2.9. Spin the tubes at 14,000 x g for 60 seconds at room temperature.
2.10. Discard the flowthrough and add IVT mRNA diluted in 500 µL chromatography buffer to each NucleoSpin column tube.
2.11. Attach the tubes to the vortex platform, shake vigorously for 30 minutes.
2.12. Transfer the flowthrough to a new collection tube or RNase-free 1.5 mL tube.
2.13. Spin the tubes at 14,000 x g for 60 seconds at room temperature.
2.14. Add 0.1 vol 3M NaOAc (pH 5.5, RNase-free) and 1 vol ice-cold isopropanol to the flowthrough.
2.15. Vortex to mix and incubate on ice for 3600 seconds.
2.16. Spin down at maximum speed for 1200 seconds at 4 °C.
2.17. Pipet out the supernatant and add 0.5 mL ice-cold 70-75% ethanol to each tube.
2.18. Spin down at maximum speed for 300 seconds at 4 °C.
2.19. Pipet out the ethanol and add another 0.5 mL ice-cold 70-75% ethanol.
2.20. Spin down at maximum speed for 300 seconds at 4 °C.
2.21. Pipet out the ethanol and dry the RNA pellets.
2.22. Add 20-40 µL RNase-free water to each pellet.
2.23. Elute RNA on ice for 2+ hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
2.24. Resuspend the RNA pellets and spec before using or storing at -80 °C.

input: To quantify protein-DNA binding dynamics genome-wide using competition ChIP in yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae). Initial Strain Production and Characterizations.   1.1 Obtain or Generate Competition ChIP Strains.     1.1.1 Design the competition ChIP strain, referring to 'Competition ChIP strain design and characterization'.     1.1.2 Engineer transformants using relevant cloning and transformation protocols for the organism of interest.     1.1.3 Construct the strain on a haploid BY4741 background, deleting BAR1 by homologous recombination using LEU2 from pRS405.     1.1.4 Generate the constitutive RAP1 allele by tagging the endogenous RAP1 locus with a 3× Flag tag from p3Flag-KanMX40.     1.1.5 Generate the competitor RAP1 allele by introducing a second RAP1 copy at the his3-1 locus, tagged with a 9× Myc tag from pYM20 and driven by a weakened galactose-inducible promoter GALL from pYM-N27.   1.2 Characterization of Competition ChIP Strain.     1.2.1 Refer to Box 4 for characterization of the competition ChIP strain. 2. ChIP Sample Preparation.   4.1 Thaw ChIP Sample Pellets.     4.1.1 Thaw ChIP sample pellets in 1 ml of ice-cold beadbeater lysis buffer.     4.1.2 Re-pellet the sample by spinning it at 15,000g for 10 s at room temperature.     4.1.3 Discard the supernatant.   4.2 Lysis and Sonication.     4.2.1 Resuspend the pellet in 0.5 ml of ice-cold beadbeater lysis buffer.     4.2.2 Add ∼1 ml of 0.5-mm glass beads.     4.2.3 Lyse cells in the Mini-BeadBeater-8 with four 1-min sessions on 'high', with 2-min pauses between sessions.     4.2.4 Recover the extract by puncturing the bottom of the 2-ml screw-top tubes with a needle.   4.3 Sonication and Centrifugation.     4.3.1 Sonicate the samples in 1.5-ml tubes using a bioruptor sonicator.     4.3.2 Spin the samples at 15,000g at 4 °C for 5 min.     4.3.3 Transfer the supernatant lysate to new 1.5-ml tubes and repeat centrifugation.

input: The objective is to consistently extract high-quality DNA from challenging plant and fungal samples. Have prepared sorbitol wash buffer, CTAB extraction buffer, and necessary reagents. How to perform the DNA extraction?
output: 1. Add an excess of sorbitol wash buffer to fill sample tubes containing macerated plant material to approximately ¾ capacity (0.9 – 1.5 ml, depending on tubes used).
2. Cap tubes and shake in the bead mill, manually or using vortex. Inspect to confirm suspension of the powdered material and shake again, if necessary.
3. Centrifuge at 5,000-6,000 x g for three minutes at room temperature.
4. The supernatant is decanted or aspirated from samples and discarded.
5. (Optional) Repeat the sorbitol wash if the supernatant from step 3 is turbid, viscous or dark with polyphenolics.
6. Add pre-warmed extraction buffer to the sample tubes (approximately ½ the sample tube capacity: 650 µl in 2 ml tubes or 400 µl when for example 1.1 ml microtubes in 96-well tube racks are used).
7. Resuspend macerate samples by shaking for five seconds in the bead mill or by vortexing.
8. Incubate samples at 65°C for a minimum of 30 minutes, up to 60 minutes, with mixing by inversion every ten minutes.
9. Remove from water bath/oven and allow samples to cool at room temperature for five minutes.
10. Add CIA to sample tubes (700 µl or fill to approximately 4/5 tube capacity).
11. Shake tubes vigorously for 10 seconds.
12. Centrifuge samples at 5,000-6,000 x g for 30 minutes at room temperature.
13. Carefully remove the upper aqueous phase by pipetting. In 2 ml tube extractions, 650 µl upper phase is usually safely recoverable.
14. Transfer to a new tube, carefully avoiding disturbance of the debris between phases.
15. Nucleic acids are precipitated by the addition of 1/10 volume of 3 M sodium acetate pH 5.2 and 0.66 volumes isopropanol.
16. Mix by inverting ten times and keep at room temperature for at least one hour or overnight.
17. Centrifuge at 13,000 x g for 30 minutes at room temperature.

system_prompt: As a specialist in Biochemical & Molecular Functional Analysis, provide clear step-by-step instructions for assaying glycogen and trehalose in yeast.
instruction: Please describe the protocol in a two-level list format (using 1., 2., 3. numbers, with one-level sub-steps). Include only the steps, not a rationale or materials list. Use concise language and maintain a chronological order.
input: The objective is to measure glycogen and trehalose in yeast using 2 ml screw-capped tubes. Have prepared cell concentration measurements and samples. Now, how to proceed with the glycogen and trehalose assays?
output: 1. Cell Concentration Measurement and Sampling.   1.1. Measure cell concentration carefully using a Coulter Counter or light scattering in a spectrophotometer.   1.2. Transfer samples containing either 5.0×10^7 cells or 1.0×10^8 cells to a 2 ml screw-capped tube.   1.3. Centrifuge at about 20,000 x g for 10 sec. 2. Cell Pellet Washing and Resuspension.   2.1. Remove the supernatant and wash the cell pellet once in 1 ml ice-cold water.   2.2. Resuspend cell pellets in 125 ul of 0.25 M Na2CO3 solution with initial vigorous vortexing. 3. Incubation at 95°C.   3.1. Incubate at 95°C for about 3h with occasional vortexing.   3.2. Maintain temperature at the top of the tube to avoid excessive condensation. 4. pH Adjustment and Volume Adjustment.   4.1. Adjust the pH to 5.5 and the volume to 0.5 ml by addition of 75 ul 1 M acetic acid and 300 ul 0.2 M NaAcetate.   4.2. Vortex the sample vigorously to resuspend and disperse cell debris. 5. Sample Division for Glycogen and Trehalose Measurements.   5.1. Divide the sample into two 250 ul aliquots for glycogen and trehalose measurements.   5.2. Note that it may be important to divide the cell debris equally. 6. Glycogen Measurement.   6.1. Make a 20 mg/ml solution of Aspergillus niger α-amyloglucosidase freshly in 0.2 M NaAcetate, pH 5.2.   6.2. Add 10 ul of the solution to the 250 ul sample and incubate overnight at 57°C. 7. Trehalose Measurement.   7.1. Adjust the pH slightly upwards by addition of 15 ul of 0.2 M NaAcetate.   7.2. Add 3 ul of porcine trehalase and mix well, then incubate overnight at 37°C. 8. Glucose Quantification.   8.1. Prepare the glucose oxidase/peroxidase/o-dianisidine reagent as described by the manufacturer.   8.2. Centrifuge cell samples and mix 50 ul of supernatant with 100 ul of assay reagent.   8.3. Incubate at 37°C for 30 min and add 100 ul of 9 N H2SO4 to stop the reaction. 9. Standard Curve Preparation and Data Analysis.   9.1. Prepare 50 ul samples of glucose standards and assay in parallel.   9.2. Measure absorbance at 540 nanometers and convert to absolute amounts of glucose using the standard curve.

system_prompt: As a CRISPR/Cas9 protocol expert, provide detailed step-by-step instructions for molecular biology procedures.
instruction: Please provide a two-level list (1., 2., 3., with sub-steps) of the protocol steps. Only include actionable steps in chronological order.
input: The aim is to expand individual iPSC clones after CRISPR/Cas9 editing. Materials include 96-well and 24-well plates. How to perform clone expansion?
output: 1. Feed iPSCs in 96-well plates daily with mTeSR + P/S. The cells are ready to be split when iPSCs in a well are almost confluent and/or individual colonies grow to a size >half of the well.
2. Splitting cells from 96-well plates to 24-well plates using Accutase:
2.1. Prepare 24-well plate(s) by coating with Matrigel GFR, then adding 500 µL mTeSR + RI + P/S per well. Place 24-well plate(s) in cell culture incubator to pre-equilibrate.

2.2. Aspirate mTeSR from all wells of the 96-well plate and wash with PBS. Then add 25 µL Accutase per well. Return to incubator and let sit for 360s - 480s. Add 200 µL mTeSR (+RI + P/S) to each well and break up bigger cell clusters by pipetting up and down 3-4 times in each well. Transfer cells from one well of the 96-well plate to one well of a 24-well plate.
3. Prepare 6-well plates by coating with Matrigel GFR, then adding 2 mL mTeSR + RI per well.

4. Aspirate mTeSR from wells in 24-well plate and wash with PBS. Add 100 µL Accutase per well and incubate at 37 °C for 360s - 480s. While cells are at 37 °C, prepare one 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube with 200 µL mTeSR + RI for each clone.
5. Aspirate cells in Accutase by pipetting up and down a few times in each well. Then add cells to prepared Eppendorf tube.

6. Spin cells down using a tabletop centrifuge (180s at 200rpm and Room temperature). Resuspend each pellet in 1 mL mTeSR + RI (taken from the prepared 6-well plate) and plate individual clones onto separate wells of 6-well plates.

system_prompt: As an expert in RNA ISH, RNA FISH, and protein-RNA double labeling techniques in Drosophila ovaries, your task is to decompose the protocol into hierarchical steps, ensuring parameter inheritance and logical cross-step coordination.
instruction: Break down the protocol into multi-level steps, starting with main steps (1-10), followed by sub-steps (≤15 per main step), and sub-sub-steps (≤15 per sub-step). Use imperative verbs for each step. Ensure reagent and equipment continuity across steps.
input: To optimize RNA detection in Drosophila ovaries, requiring high resolution and sensitivity. Available materials: wet yeast paste, EBR, 4% paraformaldehyde, ethanol, proteinase K, DIG-labeled RNA probes, antibodies, NBT/BCIP, DAPI, and microscopy equipment. How to perform RNA ISH, FISH, and protein-RNA double labeling in Drosophila ovaries?
output: 1. Setup of Fly Cultures for Ovary Dissection.   1.1. Fatten 1- to 2-d-old adult female flies by placing them with males in vials with wet yeast paste for 24–48 h at 25°C.   1.2. If female flies are less than 1-d old, fatten them for at least 48 h. 2. Dissection of Ovaries for ISH, FISH, and IF/FISH (Day 1).   2.1. Anesthetize flies on a CO2 pad.   2.2. Submerge a fly in cold 1× EBR.   2.3. Grasp the thorax and abdomen with forceps.   2.4. Tear off the posterior abdomen tip and pull out ovaries.   2.5. Transfer ovaries to fresh EBR.   2.6. Break up ovarioles with forceps.   2.7. Store dissected ovaries in EBR on ice for up to 1 h. 3. Preparation of Tissue for ISH and FISH.   3.1. Fix ovaries in 4% paraformaldehyde in 1× PBS with 1% DMSO for 1 h.   3.2. Rinse three times in 1× PBS.   3.3. Dehydrate ovaries through ethanol series: 25%, 50%, 75%, and three times in 100%. 4. Rehydration, Permeabilization, RNase Inactivation, and Probe Hybridization (Day 2).   4.1. Rehydrate through reverse ethanol series.   4.2. Permeabilize with proteinase K for 1 h.   4.3. Inactivate proteinase K with glycine.   4.4. Prepare probe by diluting DIG-labeled RNA probe in HYB solution.   4.5. Denature probe at 68°C, chill on ice, and hybridize overnight at 60°C. 5. Posthybridization Washes and Blocking (Day 3).   5.1. Wash at 65°C in HYB and PBT.   5.2. Block in PBT:WBR. 6. DIG Antibody Incubation and Signal Detection.   6.1. Incubate with digoxigenin-alkaline phosphatase antibody overnight.   6.2. Detect signal with NBT/BCIP and mount in glycerol.   6.3. Alternatively, use biotin-conjugated antibody, streptavidin-HRP, and tyramide amplification for fluorescence detection.

Prepare Pst AvrRpt2 (OD600nm=0.002) in 10 mM MgCl2 (or MgSO4) in a 15ml tube. 3. Leaf Infiltration.   3.1. Using a 1m needle-less syringe, pressure-infiltrate 3 fully expanded leaves (leaves 4, 5, and 6) per plant with the Pst AvrRpt2.   3.2. Dry excess of Pst AvrRpt2 inoculum gently using Kimwipes. 4. Plant Incubation.   4.1. Move plants to chambers set to conditions being compared.   4.2. Keep 6 plants per genotype under 50% RH, 22°C, 12 h light, 12 h dark, and the other 6 plants per genotype under 90% RH, 22°C, 12 h light/12 h dark conditions for 36h. 5. Water Collection and Confirmation.   5.1. Collect dH2O in a 1 L beaker and confirm that the conductivity is below 1.5uS/cm. 6. Leaf Disc Collection.   6.1. Using the EMS Rapid-core 6.0 puncher, collect 3 leaf discs per plant (1 disc per leaf) in a 50ml tube (i.e., 6 tubes per genotype). 7. Leaf Disc Rinsing.   7.1. Add 30ml dH2O to each tube and rinse discs by inverting tube 3 times. 8. Mannitol Preparation.   8.1. Using dH2O, prepare 100ml of 400mM mannitol (7.3g mannitol in 100ml dH2O) per genotype. 9. Make a blank by adding 6ml 400mM mannitol to an empty 50ml tube for measurement correction during data analysis. 11. Incubation and Measurement.   11.1. Shake tubes at 100 rpm for 2h at room temperature.   11.2. Using the Thermo Scientific Orion Star A322 electro-conductivity meter, measure initial ion leakage and proceed to data analysis.

input: The objective is to perform co-staining for BrdU and Ki67 for flow cytometry analysis. Have prepared the cell suspension and cryopreserved the cells. Now, how to proceed with BrdU and Ki67 staining?
output: 1. Day 1: Staining for Cell Surface Markers, Fixation, and Permeabilisation   1.1. Euthanise BrdU-treated mice by cervical dislocation and remove the organs containing the populations of interest for analysis.   1.2. Place the organs onto a piece of nylon mesh in a Petri dish containing 3ml of PBS/BSA, cover with a second piece of nylon mesh, and gently crush the organs to release the cells into the buffer.   1.3. Collect the cell suspension and transfer it to a FACS tube.   1.4. Perform cell counts and transfer 2 million total cells to FACS tubes for staining.   1.5. Wash cells by adding 1ml of PBS/BSA, centrifuge, and discard the supernatant.   1.6. Resuspend cells in 100µl of Surface Marker Antibody Cocktail and incubate for 1 hour on ice.   1.7. Wash cells again, fix, and permeabilise them by resuspending in 100µl Cytofix/Cytoperm buffer and incubating for 30 minutes on ice.   1.8. Wash cells with 1x Perm/Wash buffer, centrifuge, and discard the supernatant.   1.9. Resuspend cells in 1ml PBS/BSA and store at 4°C overnight. 2. Day 2: Co-staining for BrdU and Ki67   2.1. Recover cells from storage, centrifuge, and discard the supernatant.   2.2. Wash cells by resuspending the pellet in 1ml of freshly prepared 1x Perm/Wash buffer, centrifuge, and discard the supernatant.   2.3. Resuspend cells in 100µl Cytoperm Permeabilisation Buffer Plus and incubate for 10 minutes on ice.   2.4. Wash the Cytoperm Permeabilisation Buffer Plus off the cells, centrifuge, and discard the supernatant.   2.5. Repeat fixation by resuspending cells in 100µl of Cytofix/Cytoperm buffer and incubating for 5 minutes at room temperature.   2.6. Expose incorporated BrdU by resuspending cells in 100µl of 300µg/ml DNase and incubating for 1 hour at 37°C.   2.7. Co-stain for BrdU and Ki67 by resuspending cells in 50µl 1x Perm/Wash containing anti-BrdU FITC and anti-Ki67 eFluor660, and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.   2.8. Wash cells to remove residual unbound antibody, centrifuge, and discard the supernatant.   2.9. Acquire samples on a flow cytometer equipped with appropriate lasers and filters for the detection of FITC and eFluor660 fluorescence.

Single-Molecule Analysis.   8.1 Measure hybridization efficiency and distances between labeled sites using ImageJ. 9. input: To perform spatially resolved transcriptomic analysis in human brain sections using DART-FISH. Available materials: Silicone isolators, EasyDip jars, HybEZ oven, formaldehyde, PFA, PBST, ethanol, padlock probes, RNase, cDNA crosslinker, RCA enzymes, acryloyl-X mix, polymerization mix, DEPC-1X PBS, Draq5. How to prepare, permeabilize, hybridize, and image DART-FISH samples?
output: 1. Reparation.
1.1. Wash, dry, and UV the silicone isolators.
1.2. UV the EasyDip jars.
1.3. Clean the working area and set the HybEZ oven to 37°C.
2. Permeabilization.
2.1. Prepare 75ml of 4% formaldehyde in 1x PBS.
2.2. Insert sections on coverslips into the staining jar containing 4% PFA in PBS. Fix for 60 mins at 4°C.
2.3. Incubate samples in 1x PBST at 4°C for 3 mins, then at room temperature for 3 mins.
3. Probe Preparation.
3.1. Ensure padlock probes have 5' phosphate. If not, run T4 PNK reaction and clean up using Zymo columns.
4. Dehydration and Mounting.
4.1. Prepare jars of 50%, 70%, and two 100% ethanol. Dehydrate sections through ethanol steps.
4.2. Mount coverslips on silicone isolators and seal completely.
5. Permeabilization.
5.1. Permeabilize samples with 0.25% Triton X-100 in DEPC-1X PBS for 10 mins.
5.2. Wash samples thrice with DEPC-1X PBS and DEPC-H2O.
6. Reverse Transcription.
6.1. Prepare Reverse Transcription Mix on ice. Incubate sections with the mix for 10 mins at 4°C, then 5 mins at 37°C.
6.2. Wash with 1X PBS twice.
7. cDNA Crosslinking.
7.1. Crosslink cDNAs with BS(PEG)9. Prepare 5mM BS(PEG)9 in PBS. Crosslink for 1 hour at room temperature. Wash with PBS twice.
7.2. Quench unreacted crosslinker with 1M Tris, pH 8.0 for 30 mins at room temperature. Wash with PBS twice.
8. RNase Digestion.
8.1. Prepare RNase Digestion Mix. Incubate at 37°C for 1 hour.
8.2. Wash samples with 1X PBS twice.
9. Padlock Probe Hybridization.
9.1. Prepare the 484-gene Hybridization Mix. Preheat probe-water mix to 85°C for 3 mins, then move to ice. Complete the Hybridization Mix.
9.2. Incubate samples in the Hybridization Mix at 37°C for 30 mins, then at 55°C for 0 mins.
10. RCA.
10.1. Prepare RCA Primer Mix. Incubate at 37°C for 1 hour.
10.2. Wash samples with 2X SSC twice.
10.3. Prepare RCA Enzyme Mix on ice. Add to samples and incubate at 30°C for 5 hours.
11. Padlock Probe Hybridization.
11.1. Wash samples with 1X PBS twice.
12. RCA.
12.1. Wash samples with 1X PBS twice.
13. Rolony Crosslinking.
13.1. Crosslink with Acryloyl-X Mix and embed in gel. Prepare Acrylamide Solution. Aspirate the solution without washing.
13.2. Prepare Polymerization Mix. Add to samples and cover with Gel-Slick-treated coverslips for 30 mins at room temperature.
13.3. Wash with 1X PBST for 3 mins twice. Remove coverslips and repeat washing.
14. Imaging.
14.1. Stain samples with Probe Hybridization Mix containing decoding probes (e.g., dcProbe0_AF488, dcProbe0_Cy3, dcProbe0_ATTO647N). Incubate for 8 mins at room temperature.
14.2. Wash with 10% formamide in 2X SSC twice. Image samples.
14.3. Strip with 80% formamide in 2X SSC for 5 mins. Wash with 2X SSC once. Repeat imaging with next decoding probes.
15. Pepsin Digestion.
15.1. Wash samples with DEPC-1X PBS twice.
15.2. Digest with 0.01% Pepsin in 0.1N HCl. Pre-warm pepsin to 37°C for 5 mins before use. Incubate for 1.5 mins at 37°C.
16. Imaging.
16.1. Add Draq5 solution to samples. Incubate for 5 mins at room temperature.
16.2. Wash with 1X PBS twice. Image nuclei staining.

output: 1. Multi-well Plate Strainer Insert Preparation.   1.1 3D-print the Tinkercad-designed multi-well plate strainer insert.   1.2 Set a hot plate to medium heat.   1.3 Prepare Nylon Mesh.     1.3.1 Cut rectangles of nylon mesh, approximately 9cm×12cm.     1.3.2 Fold a piece of aluminum foil into a double-layer.   1.4 Assemble and Seal the Insert.     1.4.1 Place the double layer of aluminum foil on the hot plate.     1.4.2 Place a rectangle of nylon mesh on top of the aluminum foil.     1.4.3 Press the 3D-printed multi-well insert into the nylon mesh, applying pressure for 3 seconds.     1.4.4 Press around the edge of each well to form a complete seal.   1.5 Post-Assembly Processing.     1.5.1 Press the insert into the nylon mesh for 3 more seconds on the benchtop.     1.5.2 Gently peel off the foil from the insert.     1.5.3 Check the bottom of each well for a complete seal.     1.5.4 Repeat steps as necessary until a complete seal is achieved.   1.6 Trimming and Quality Control.     1.6.1 Use small scissors to cut away excess nylon mesh between wells.     1.6.2 Feel around the bottom of each well to ensure the seal has not been compromised.   1.7 Sterilization and Storage.     1.7.1 Submerge the inserts in 10% bleach solution for 20-24 hours.     1.7.2 Transfer the inserts to distilled water for soaking up to 24 hours.     1.7.3 Air dry the inserts and store in a clean plastic bag. 2. Zebrafish Embryo Preparation.   2.1 Day -1: Set Up Crosses.     2.1.1 Place healthy zebrafish into breeding tanks, separating females and males.   2.2 Day 0: Water Change, Execute Crossing, Collect Embryos.     2.2.1 Refresh the water in breeding tanks when lights turn on.     2.2.2 Remove breeding dividers and execute crossing.     2.2.3 Observe fish until spawning begins and viable embryos are produced.     2.2.4 Prepare a bleach solution (100uL bleach in 150mL ICS water).     2.2.5 Recover embryos using a strainer.     2.2.6 Rinse embryos in bleach solution using an ICS water squirt bottle.     2.2.7 Leave embryos in bleach solution for 10 minutes, swirling intermittently.     2.2.8 Rinse embryos thoroughly in ICS water.     2.2.9 Partition embryos into Petri dishes, aiming for 100 embryos per dish.   2.3 Day 1: Sort Embryos.     2.3.1 Under a dissecting microscope, transfer viable embryos to new Petri dishes.     2.3.2 Aim for 50-60 embryos per Petri dish.     2.3.3 Place Petri dishes in an incubator overnight at 28.5°C.   2.4 Day 3-4: Dechorionate.     2.4.1 Remove chorions from larvae using fine-tipped tweezers.     2.4.2 Place remaining larvae in Petri dishes and incubate overnight at 28.5°C. 3. Drug Treatment and Imaging.   3.1 Sanitize lab space with ethanol.   3.2 Prepare Drug Treatments.     3.2.1 Prepare appropriate working concentrations of drugs.     3.2.2 Transfer drug treatments into respective wells of a multi-well plate.     3.2.3 Label each plate.   3.3 Prepare Larvae for Treatment.     3.3.1 Pour larvae into a cell strainer and place in a Petri dish with ICS water.     3.3.2 Place the multi-well plate-strainer insert in a large Petri dish full of water.     3.3.3 Transfer larvae into each well of the insert.   3.4 Drug Treatment.     3.4.1 Incubate larvae in drug treatment for the desired exposure time.     3.4.2 Warm ICS water to 28°C and thaw Tricaine stock during treatment.   3.5 YO-PRO-1 Staining.     3.5.1 Thaw YO-PRO-1 solution one hour before larvae finish drug treatment.     3.5.2 Prepare YO-PRO-1 solution in a glass bottle or 50mL tube covered in foil.     3.5.3 Transfer YO-PRO-1 solution into each well of a new multi-well plate, cover with foil, and place in a 28°C incubator until end of drug treatment.   3.6 Post-Treatment Processing.     3.6.1 Fill a tub with fresh ICS water for washing.     3.6.2 Remove the drug treatment plate from the incubator after desired exposure time.     3.6.3 Dunk each multi-well strainer insert into the washing tub three times to wash off residual drug treatment.   3.7 Imaging.     3.7.1 Transfer inserts into the YO-PRO-1 plate.     3.7.2 Cover with foil and incubate for 20 minutes.     3.7.3 Dunk inserts into the washing tub three times to wash off residual YO-PRO-1 stain.     3.7.4 Transfer larvae to an untreated 96-well imaging plate using a P200 pipette.     3.7.5 Image larvae using a fluorescence microscope with a robotics-assisted stage.   3.8 Euthanasia.     3.8.1 Transfer extra larvae into empty wells of the imaging plate.     3.8.2 Add about 200uL of Tricaine euthanasia solution to each fish-containing well.     3.8.3 After at least 10 minutes, put the plates in a -20°C freezer for secondary euthanasia.

input: The objective is to synthesize Fmoc-Lys(N3)-OH and TEV-biotin tag for TOP-ABPP. Have prepared sodium azide solution, trifluoromethanesulfonic anhydride, and Rink amide MBHA resin. How to proceed with the synthesis?
output: 1. Synthesis of Fmoc-Lys(N3)-OH.   1.1. Add sodium azide (1.0 g, 16 mmol, 8 equiv.) to a 50 ml round-bottom flask equipped with a magnetic stir bar.   1.2. Add 2.5 ml of dichloromethane (CH2Cl2) to dissolve and cool to 0 °C in an ice bath.   1.3. Add trifluoromethanesulfonic anhydride (1.4 ml, 8 mmol, 4 equiv.) dropwise to the flask with stirring at 0 °C.   1.4. Stir at 0 °C for 2 h and quench the reaction with saturated sodium bicarbonate solution (5 ml).   1.5. Transfer the mixture to a glass separation funnel and collect the lower layer (CH2Cl2) in an Erlenmeyer flask (50 ml).   1.6. Wash the top aqueous layer with CH2Cl2 (2 × 5 ml) and combine all CH2Cl2 washes (∼10–12 ml) with the CH2Cl2 layer from Step 4.   1.7. Purify the residue by dissolving in a minimal amount of CH2Cl2 and adding to the top of a silica gel layer (∼10 cm) in the glass chromatography column.   1.8. Add 100 ml of CH2Cl2 and allow the solvent to drain from the column. 2. Synthesis of the TEV-biotin tag.   2.1. Weigh out 500 mg of Rink amide MBHA resin (500 mg, 0.3 mmol, 1 equiv.) and transfer to a 10 ml glass, fritted, peptide-synthesis vessel.   2.2. Swell the resin by adding 5 ml of CH2Cl2 to the resin and agitate by bubbling N2 gas through the inlet for 5 min.   2.3. Deprotect the Fmoc group on the resin by adding a solution of 20% piperidine/DMF (5 ml) and agitate by bubbling N2 for 5 min.   2.4. Remove the piperidine/DMF mixture by vacuum filtration, and add a fresh 5 ml of the same solution and repeat (3 × 5 min in total).   2.5. Weigh out the Fmoc-Lys(N3)-OH (260 mg, 0.7 mmol, 2 equiv.) from Step 10 and benzotriazole-1-yl-oxy-tris-pyrrolidino-phosphonium hexafluorophosphate (340 mg, 0.7 mmol, 2 equiv.) into a glass vial.   2.6. Dissolve in DMF (3 ml) and add this premixed solution to the resin.   2.7. Transfer the resin to a glass vial and add a premixed solution of 90% TFA/5% CH2Cl2/2.5% water/2.5% triethylsilane (5 ml total volume).   2.8. Incubate this cleavage reaction at room temperature for 2 h and agitate briefly by shaking every 30 min.   2.9. Transfer the cleavage mixture into a glass pipette with a plug of glass wool to filter off the resin.   2.10. Collect the flow-through in a glass vial and remove the TFA under a stream of nitrogen.

system_prompt: As a Cell Biology expert specializing in direct reprogramming of mouse embryonic fibroblasts to conventional type 1 dendritic cells, structure the protocol into hierarchical operational steps with parameter inheritance. instruction: Structure the protocol into hierarchical operational steps with parameter inheritance. Use imperative verbs, maintain tense consistency, and ensure reagent continuity across steps. Exclude theoretical explanations. Format steps as: [MainStep] [SubStep] [SubSubStep] with numeric identifiers.
input: To generate functional induced dendritic cells (iDCs) with conventional type 1 dendritic cell (cDC1) properties. Available materials: mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs), lentiviruses (FUW-TetO-PIB, FUW-M2rtTA), polybrene, DOX. How to reprogram MEFs into cDC1-like cells using transcription factors?
output: 1. Mouse Embryonic Fibroblast Isolation.   1.1 Setup and Dissection.     1.1.1 Set up timed matings for wild-type mice.     1.1.2 Check for vaginal plugs and isolate plugged females.     1.1.3 Confirm pregnancy at E13.5 and sacrifice females via CO2 inhalation.   1.2 Embryo Dissection and Cell Isolation.     1.2.1 Disinfect abdomen and dissect abdominal cavity.     1.2.2 Isolate uterus and transfer to 50ml tube with 30ml ice-cold PBS.     1.2.3 Wash uterus twice with PBS and transfer to 100mm dish.   1.3 Cell Dissociation and Plating.     1.3.1 Make incision along uterine horns to isolate sacs.     1.3.2 Separate embryos from placentas and cut-open sacs.     1.3.3 Transfer embryos to new 100mm dish with 5ml chilled PBS.   1.4 Cell Culture and Expansion.     1.4.1 Remove embryo heads and dissect visceral organs.     1.4.2 Transfer embryos to new dish and cut into small pieces.     1.4.3 Add 1.5ml dissociation solution per embryo and incubate at 37°C for 20min.   1.5 Cell Purification and Freezing.     1.5.1 Add additional 3ml dissociation solution and pipette up and down.     1.5.2 Incubate at 37°C for 20min and add 6ml DMEM complete medium.     1.5.3 Pipette up and down a few times and incubate for 5min at room temperature.   1.6 Cell Filtering and Centrifugation.     1.6.1 Filter supernatant through 40um cell strainer.     1.6.2 Centrifuge at 350xg for 5min and discard supernatant.     1.6.3 Resuspend cell pellet in 10ml fresh complete medium.   1.7 Cell Counting and Plating.     1.7.1 Count cells and adjust concentration to 10^6 cells/ml.     1.7.2 Pre-coat 100mm dish with 5ml 0.1% gelatin solution.     1.7.3 Aspirate gelatin solution and transfer 10ml cell suspension to dish. 2. Lentiviral Production.   2.1 Cell Culture and Transfection.     2.1.1 Expand HEK 293T cells in 150mm plates with 20ml DMEM medium.     2.1.2 Remove medium, wash once with PBS, and dissociate with 6ml TrypLE Express.     2.1.3 Add 6ml DMEM medium and resuspend cells by pipetting up and down.   2.2 Viral Harvest and Concentration.     2.2.1 Harvest viral supernatants at 36h, 48h, and 60h post-transfection.     2.2.2 Filter supernatants through 0.45um PES filter system.     2.2.3 Pipette 12ml filtered supernatant into Amicon ultra-15 centrifugal filter unit.   2.3 Viral Aliquoting and Storage.     2.3.1 Prepare aliquots in microtubes on ice (50-200ul) of each type of concentrated lentiviruses.     2.3.2 Store at -80°C for long-term storage or 4°C for short-term storage. 3. Dendritic Cell Reprogramming.   3.1 Cell Thawing and Plating.     3.1.1 Thaw MEF vials at 37°C and add cells dropwise into 10ml pre-warmed DMEM medium.     3.1.2 Centrifuge at 350xg for 5min and aspirate supernatant.     3.1.3 Resuspend cell pellet in 10ml DMEM complete medium per vial.   3.2 Lentiviral Transduction.     3.2.1 Replace medium with 10ml DMEM medium supplemented with polybrene (8ug/ml) and 30-60ul 1:1 mix of FUW-TetO-PIB and FUW-M2rtTA lentiviruses.     3.2.2 Incubate overnight at 37°C with 5% CO2.     3.2.3 Perform second lentiviral transduction as described in Step C6.   3.3 Cell Culture and Analysis.     3.3.1 Replace media with fresh DMEM medium supplemented with DOX (1ug/ml).     3.3.2 Replace culture media with DMEM medium supplemented with DOX every 2-3 days for 9 days.     3.3.3 Analyze emergence of iDCs during DC reprogramming at different time points.

input: To analyze phototactic responses in Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 at macroscopic and microscopic scales. input: Goal: Subculture confluent mammalian cells from T-25 flask. Completed cell confluency assessment and washing. Next steps for cell detachment, processing, and reseeding?
output: 1. Inspect cells under light microscope to evaluate confluency levels.
2. Perform cell washing procedure.

2.2. Aspirate DPBS and place in waste beaker.

3.1. Introduce 1 mL warmed trypsin-EDTA solution.
3.2. Wait 5 minutes for cells to detach.

4. Harvest cell suspension.
4.1. Transfer cell mixture to 15 mL centrifuge tube.

5.1. Discard supernatant and place in waste beaker.
5.2. Remove remaining media with 1000 µL pipette, avoiding cell disruption.
5.3. Resuspend pellet in 1000 µL fresh media, let sit for 1 minute.
5.4. Gently mix suspension to achieve homogeneous cell distribution.
6. Transfer cells to fresh flask.
6.1. Add 500 µL cell suspension to new T-25 flask.
6.2. Supplement flask with 3.5 mL fresh media to retain any residual cells.
7. Incubate flask at 37 °C in CO2 incubator to support cell growth.

input: To safely capture and sample small nonhuman primates in their natural habitat using multi-compartment traps, administer anesthesia, and ensure same-day release. Available materials include multi-compartment traps, anesthetic syringes, disinfectants, and recovery cages. How to prepare, capture, process, and release the primates while minimizing stress and ensuring rapid recovery?
output: 1. Preparatory Phase.
1.1 Check trap functionality the day before capture.
1.1.1 Inspect trap compartments for sharp points; remove or cover as necessary.
1.1.2 Test manual pull system for multi-compartment traps; ensure strings are properly tied to doors and secured to trees.
1.2 Pack all necessary materials and equipment for trapping and processing.
1.3 Assemble processing tent approximately 50 meters from trap site, ensuring it is out of direct visibility.
2. Trapping.
2.1 Monitor trap with team members using binoculars and walkie-talkies.
2.1.1 Notify processing tent when target primates are at the trap.
2.2 Capture primates one at a time using manual pull system.
2.2.1 Maintain tension on strings to prevent doors from falling or being pushed open.
2.3 For group capture, wait until all individuals have entered the trap.
2.3.1 If some animals are not entering, decide whether to leave them outside or abort the capture.
2.4 Once all animals are trapped, secure all trap doors closed before approaching.
3. 1st Phase - Processing.
3.1 Administer anesthetic intramuscularly using pre-labeled syringes.
3.1.1 Restrain animal with towel and leather glove while injecting.
3.2 Move animal into processing tent for initial assessment.
3.2.1 Record weight using digital handheld scale; note empty bag weight.
3.3 Collect initial samples: hair, nails, buccal swabs.
3.4 Monitor animal's vital signs and ensure proper sedation level.
4. 1st Phase - Sampling.
4.1 Collect hair samples from left flank; store in labeled bags.
4.2 Collect nail samples from each hand and foot.
4.3 Collect buccal swabs using plastic swab; store in tubes with preservative.
5. Recovery & Finalization.
5.1 Move animals to recovery cage; cover with sheets to maintain quiet, dark environment.
5.2 Monitor recovery every 10 minutes; collect any fecal or urine samples.
5.3 Offer banana pieces through cage mesh to assess readiness for release.
6. Release.
6.1 Open compartments consecutively to allow animals to exit one at a time.
6.2 Document release event with video and individual photos.
7. Data Organization and Entry.
7.1 Upload processing sheet data to online ODK form.
7.2 Write detailed trapping report and organize photos/videos into designated folders.

Format steps as: [MainStep] [SubStep] [SubSubStep] with numeric identifiers.
input: To isolate high-quality nuclei from flash-frozen human retinal tissue for snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq. Available materials: razor blades, glass dounce homogenizer, RNAse-free lysis buffer, 40um Flumi Cell Strainers, 2ml Eppendorf tubes, RNase-free lysis buffer, DAPI, trypan blue. How to isolate nuclei, process fresh eye samples, and prepare for sequencing?
output: 1. Nuclei Isolation.
1.1. Cool on ice the following items: razor blades, glass dounce homogenizer (1ml), and RNAse-free lysis buffer.
1.2. Using the pre-cooled razor blade, cut a block (size of rice grain) of frozen retina in a dish on dry ice, and mince the tissue as small as possible.
1.3. Add 500ul ice-cold RNAse-free lysis buffer on wet ice. Start the timer.
1.4. Pipet the tissue in lysis buffer 10 times with a P1000 pipet (set to 500ul) to disrupt the tissue on wet ice. Transfer the tissue to the precooled glass dounce.
1.5. Dounce the sample 10 times with loose pestle and 10 times with tight pestle, slowly and gently while avoiding bubble generation.
1.6. Leave on ice for 3 minutes total.
1.7. Filter the sample through 40um Flumi Cell Strainers into a 2ml ice-cold Eppendorf tube.
2. Human Fresh Eye Collection and Dissection.

2.1. Remove optic nerve stalk with blade and orbital fat with forceps from the eye. Place the eye in a vial filled with 1X PBS. Label the vial with essential information. Note: Only eyes within 6 hr post-mortem should be used.
2.2. The eyes are kept on Kimwipes wet by PBS in a dish and measure its sagittal, transverse, and axial diameters using a caliper. Place the eye in a cuvette to take fundus and OCT images.

2.3. Place the eye on a folded wet Kimwipe or a piece of wet gauze to keep it stable. Gently make an incision just beneath the limbus with a new blade under the microscope, use a serrated forceps to keep the eye stable.

2.4. Use dissection scissors to cut all the way around the limbus and remove the anterior segment (cornea, lens, and iris). Separate the lens, cornea, and iris with forceps, and place them into different tubes. Take note if the lens is artificial.

2.5. Make 4 cuts with dissection scissors between the attachment points of the eye muscles, and flatten the eye such that it consists of 4 separate lobes of tissue. Carefully trim away as much vitreous as possible without disturbing the retina using VANNAS scissors.

2.6. With a 2mm punch biopsy tool centered over the fovea, press down to make an incision. With a 4mm punch biopsy tool centered over the macula, press down to make an incision. Carefully transfer the fovea and macula (no RPE or other tissues) into separate 2ml Punch tubes. Label and place the tubes in liquid nitrogen immediately and store at -80℃ overnight.

2.7. Use a razor blade to make an “X” to separate the lobes, and number the lobes clockwise as 1-4, starting with the lobe containing the macula. For each lobe, separate the retinal and RPE/choroid layers using forceps carefully. Store each sample (4 retinal lobes and 4 RPE/choroid lobes, totally 8 samples) in a 2ml tube. Label and place the tubes in liquid nitrogen immediately and store at -80℃ overnight.
2.8. Collect the remaining tissue in a 15ml Falcon tube. Label and place the tube in liquid nitrogen immediately and store at -80℃ overnight. This tissue can be used for DNA extraction.
3. Nuclei Isolation.
3.1. Proceed to 10X snRNA-seq/10X snATAC-seq.
3.2. Disinfect the bench with 70% ethanol and clean up the work area. Rinse tools in water before placing them in a container with 70% ethanol.

3.3. For snRNA-seq, add DAPI (1ug/ml) and then FACS sort for nuclei immediately. Count the nuclei concentration. The final concentration should be 800-1000 nuclei/ul. The nuclei are ready for 10X snRNA-seq. For snATAC-seq, spin down the sample at 500 g for 5 min at 4℃. Remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet and resuspend the pellet in 50ul diluted Nuclei Buffer (1X). Stain the nuclei with trypan blue and count the concentration. The final concentration should be 3000-5000 nuclei/ul.

system_prompt: As a Cell Biology expert specializing in angiogenesis assays, you are tasked with structuring a hierarchical protocol for an in vitro tube formation assay using endothelial cells and basement membrane extract.
instruction: Organize the provided protocol into a multi-level structure with imperative verbs, ensuring each step is concise and maintains numerical consistency. Exclude theoretical explanations and focus on operational steps.
input: To study in vitro angiogenesis, endothelial cells are plated on gelled basement membrane extract to form capillary-like tubes. Materials include HUVECs, basement membrane extract, growth media (EBM-2, EGM-2), and various reagents (bFGF, Sulforaphane, Calcein AM). The goal is to measure tube formation efficiency under different conditions.
output: 1. Passaging of Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cells   1.1 Split nearly confluent flasks of HUVECs such that cells will be ∼80% confluent in 24 h. Generally, plating 5 × 10^5 to 1 × 10^6 cells in a 25-cm^2 flask works well. 2. Thawing the Basement Membrane Extract   2.1 Remove the basement membrane extract from the −20 °C or −80 °C freezer and place it in a refrigerator at 4 °C. 3. Coating 96-Well Cell Culture Plate with Basement Membrane Extract   3.1 Label wells (in triplicate) of 96-well plate as follows: EBM-2, EBM-2 with 35 ng ml–1 bFGF, EGM-2, and EGM-2 with 15 μM Sulforaphane.   3.2 Place a tube of fully thawed basement membrane extract and labeled 96-well plate on ice in a laminar flow hood. Invert the tube with extract a few times to mix the contents.   3.3 Load 50–80 μl of the basement membrane extract per well of 96-well plate.   3.4 Transfer 96-well plate to a cell culture incubator and incubate it at 37 °C for 30 min to allow the basement membrane to gel. 4. Harvesting 80% Confluent HUVECs from 25-cm^2 Flask   4.1 Warm PBS, trypsin–EDTA, EGM-2, and EBM-2 in the 37 °C water bath.   4.2 Remove and discard the media from 25-cm^2 flask with HUVECs and rinse cells with PBS.   4.3 Add 1 ml of trypsin–EDTA to the flask, swirl briefly, and incubate at 37 °C for a few minutes to release the cells.   4.4 Tap the side of the flask to be sure that the cells are detaching. 5. Quantitating and Collecting Cells   5.1 Add 1 ml of growth medium EGM-2; gently pipette the solution up and down to make a single cell suspension.   5.2 Transfer cell suspension in a sterile 15 ml conical tube.   5.3 Determine cell number and viability by mixing 5 μl of cell suspension with 5 μl of Trypan blue and using a hemocytometer.   5.4 Centrifuge cells at 200 × g for 3 min in a centrifuge with a swing-bucket rotor. 6. Preparing Cells for Assay   6.1 Aspirate supernatant and resuspend cell pellet in a basal medium EBM-2 at a concentration of 1.5 × 10^5 cells per 1 ml.   6.2 Label four sterile 15 ml conical tubes as follows: EBM-2, EBM-2 with 35 ng ml–1 bFGF, EGM-2, and EGM-2 with 15 μM Sulforaphane.   6.3 Load 1 ml (1.5 × 10^5 cells) of a single cell suspension in each tube.   6.4 Centrifuge the tubes for 3 min at 200 × g and aspirate the supernatant.   6.5 Add the corresponding medium to cell pellets as follows: 1 ml basal medium EBM-2, 1 ml basal medium EBM-2 and 3.5 μl of 10 ng μl–1 bFGF stock solution, 1 ml complete medium EGM-2 and 1.5 μl DMSO, and 1 ml complete medium EGM-2 and 1.5 μl of 10 mM Sulforaphane stock solution.   6.6 Carefully resuspend cell pellets in the medium to make single cell suspensions at a concentration of 1.5 × 10^5 cells per ml. 7. Putting Cells on Top of Gelled Basement Membrane Extract to Begin the Assay   7.1 Gently add 100 μl (15,000 cells) per well of the single cell suspensions prepared in Steps 14 and 15 to corresponding labeled wells of a 96-well plate on top of the gelled basement membrane extract.   7.2 Incubate 96-well plate at 37 °C, 5% CO2 in the cell culture incubator for a period of 4–16 h, or until the desired result is achieved.   7.3 Examine the plate every hour for tube formation under an inverted microscope with ×4 or ×10 objective. 8. Labeling and Imaging/Quantitating Cells   8.1 Photograph the tubular network in the wells using a digital camera attached to an inverted microscope with ×4 or ×10 objective.   8.2 Aspirate the medium from the wells, add 100 μl of warm DPBS, and immediately photograph the wells.   8.3 Replacing the medium with DPBS solution can be necessary if the medium contains phenol red and the color reduces the quality of the pictures.   8.4 Prepare 6 μM of Calcein AM by adding 3 μl of 2 mM Calcein AM stock solution to 1 ml EBM-2 medium.   8.5 Without aspirating the medium, add 50 μl of 6 μM Calcein AM solution per well of the 96-well plate.   8.6 Incubate the plate at 37 °C and in 5% CO2 for 15–30 min.   8.7 Calcein AM-labeled cells should be observed and photographed using a fluorescent inverted microscope with 485 nm excitation or 520 nm emission filter.   8.8 Make 2 μM Calcein AM solution in DPBS as follows: 1 μl of 2 mM Calcein AM stock solution per 1 ml of DPBS.   8.9 Aspirate the medium from the wells and add 100 μl of 2 μM Calcein AM solution per well of 96-well plate.   8.10 Incubate the plate for 15–30 min at 37 °C in 5% CO2.   8.11 Photograph Calcein AM-labeled cells using fluorescent inverted microscope with 485 nm excitation or 520 nm emission filter.   8.12 Aspirate the medium from the wells and rinse the wells three times with 100 μl of PBS per well.   8.13 Aspirate the last wash, add 100 μl of −20 °C cold methanol per well, and incubate the plate for 30 s to 1 min.   8.14 Aspirate methanol and immediately rinse the wells three times with distilled H2O.   8.15 Aspirate last wash, add 100 μl of cell staining solution per well, and incubate the plate for 15–30 min at room temperature (21 °C).   8.16 Rinse the wells three times with distilled H2O.   8.17 Endothelial cells can be photographed, and images can be used for quantitation.

input: To purify high molecular weight (HMW) DNA from fungal samples for long-read sequencing. Available materials: Pectinase, RNase A, Proteinase K, Phenol/Chloroform/Isoamyl alcohol, 3 M Sodium Acetate (pH 5.2), Isopropanol, 70% Ethanol, TE buffer pH8.0, Qubit, Nanodrop, 0.8% Agarose gel with lambda HindIII ladder. How to isolate HMW DNA from fungi with high polysaccharide content?
output: 1. Enzyme Treatment and Volume Adjustment.
1.1. Add 80 µl Pectinase and 1 µl RNase A to 200 µl DNA solution.
1.2. Mix by gentle pipetting.
1.3. Incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
1.4. Add 2 µl Proteinase K.
1.5. Incubate at 37°C for 15 minutes.
1.6. Adjust volume to 500 µl with water.
2. Extraction with Phenol/Chloroform/Isoamyl Alcohol.
2.1. Add 500 µl Phenol/Chloroform/Isoamyl alcohol.
2.2. Invert by hand 100 times.
2.3. Centrifuge at 13000g for 10 minutes.
2.4. Transfer the aqueous phase to a new tube.
2.5. Repeat extraction two more times.
3. DNA Precipitation and Washing.
3.1. Transfer the aqueous phase to a new tube labeled as 1.
3.2. Measure the volume, typically 400 µl.
3.3. Add 1/10 volume of 3 M Sodium Acetate (pH 5.2).
3.4. Add 1 volume of isopropanol.
3.5. Invert until cotton-fiber-like DNA precipitates form.
3.6. When precipitates sediment, transfer supernatant to a new tube labeled as 2.
3.7. Add 1 ml of 70% ethanol to tube 1 containing DNA.
3.8. Centrifuge both tubes at 13000g for 5 minutes.
3.9. Wash the pellet in 1 ml of 70% ethanol.
3.10. Repeat washing two more times.
4. DNA Elution and Concentration Adjustment.
4.1. After final wash, spin at 13000g for 1 minute.
4.2. Remove ethanol.
4.3. Air dry the pellet for less than 5 minutes.
4.4. Dissolve the pellet in TE buffer pH8.0 or 10 mM Tris pH8.0.
4.5. Use 200 µl or less for tube 1 and 50-100 µl for tube 2.
4.6. Incubate at room temperature for 2-3 hours or overnight at 4°C.
5. DNA Quality Assessment.
5.1. Measure DNA concentration using Qubit and Nanodrop.
5.2. Check DNA integrity using 0.8% agarose gel with lambda HindIII ladder.

system_prompt: As a specialist in Molecular Biology Techniques, provide clear, step-by-step instructions for eDNA extraction protocols using STERIVEX filters.
instruction: Please describe the eDNA extraction protocol in a two-level list format (using 1., 2., 3. numbers, with one-level sub-steps). Include only the operating steps, not explanations or materials lists. Use concise, active voice and maintain chronological order.
input: The objective is to efficiently extract eDNA from STERIVEX filters in freshwater samples. Have completed initial sample collection and filter preparation. How to proceed with the eDNA extraction process?
output: 1. Clean the laminar flow hood and micropipettes with DNAZAP, wiping with ddH2O and 70% Ethanol using tissue paper.
2. Place gloves, sleeves, 1.5 mL (8) and 2.0 mL (24) LoBind tubes in the laminar flow hood, exposing them to UV light for 10 minutes.
3. Wipe the outer surfaces of filter capsules with 5% bleach, then dry and wipe with 70% Ethanol using tissue paper.
4. Remove the yellow inlet caps from the capsules and transfer the buffer into a 2 mL LoBind tube using a 3 mL Luer-Lock syringe.
5. Label and store the EtOH buffer in LoBind tubes at -80°C for future analysis.
6. Prepare the lysis premix by adding 900 μL ATL buffer and 100 μL proteinase K per sample in a 10 mL tube.
7. Add 1000 μL Lysis working solution to each filter, pipetting between the filter and capsule walls.
8. Seal the filter with parafilm and shake vigorously for a few seconds, then transfer to a sterile petri dish.
9. Incubate the filters in an incubator at 56°C for 24 hours without rotating, shaking vigorously in between.
10. Remove all liquid from the yellow inlet end of the capsule using a 2 mL Luer-Lock syringe, transferring to two 2 mL LoBind tubes.
11. Add Buffer AL and ice cold ethanol to the sample in equal volumes, mixing thoroughly.
12. Pipet the mixture into a DNeasy Mini Spin column in a 2 mL collection tube, spinning at 8000 rpm for 1 minute at 4°C.
13. Discard the flow-through and repeat until all sample is filtered through the spin column.
14. Place the spin column in a new 2 mL collection tube, adding 500 μL Buffer AW1 and centrifuging for 1 minute.
15. Discard the flow-through and collection tube, placing the spin column in a new 2 mL tube.
16. Add 500 μL Buffer AW2, centrifuging for 3 minutes at 14,000 rpm to dry the membrane.
17. Heat AE buffer to 70°C on a thermomixer, placing tubes with spin columns on a 70°C heating plate.
18. Add 75 μL 70°C Buffer AE to the membrane, immediately removing it and letting it stand at room temperature for 10 minutes.
19. Centrifuge for 1 minute at 8000 rpm, discarding the spin column.
20. Aliquot 30 μL of the eluate eDNA into a labeled PCR tube for DNA measurement and PCR, storing at 4°C.
21. Store the remaining 45 μL of eluate eDNA at -80°C for long-term storage.
